a: At the very front: every dB of loss before the LNA adds about 1 dB of NF, and the LNA's own NF (~0.55 dB) plus ~0.9 dB of filter loss gives ~1.5 dB after the LNA. The rest of the chain, including the ~27 dB-NF ADC behind ~33 dB of gain, adds under 1 dB by Friis, for ~2.4 dB total.
tags: tx rx fundamentals rct aau measurements

q: The TX chain loses about 50 dB before the PA. Why design it that way?
a: The FHGW, mid-board and RFFEs are separate boards joined by flexible-PCB cables. Each run costs ~13–16 dB, and a 4-way divider splits one signal to four PA paths. Gain stages are placed to make up the loss while keeping each stage in its linear range, and a variable attenuator gives ≥ 6 dB of trim for temperature and flatness.
tags: tx rx fundamentals rct aau measurements

q: Output power is 3 dB low on one of four PA paths only. Where do you look?
a: Something local to that path: its RFFE gain stage, phase-shifter or V-ATT state, PA, coupler/circulator or the connector to its filter. Shared stages (DAC, first FPCB, mid-board) would affect all four. Compare the DPD ORX level on that path to see whether the loss is before or after the coupler.
tags: tx rx fundamentals rct aau measurements

q: Why does the ADC sit ~60 dB below full scale at sensitivity?
a: That gap is the headroom for everything stronger than the weakest wanted signal: other UEs, interferers and blockers, plus the signal's own PAPR. The design keeps the maximum near −15 dBFS and switches in a 10 dB step at high input so the ADC never clips.
tags: tx rx fundamentals rct aau measurements

q: ACLR passes but EVM fails. What does that tell you?
a: The problem is in-band only, not a spreading non-linearity. Suspects: CFR clipping too hard, phase noise (points smeared along arcs), IQ imbalance or LO leakage, a converter noise floor (EVM flat vs power), or edge-subcarrier distortion from filter group delay. PA compression would normally hurt ACLR too.
tags: tx rct measurements fundamentals troubleshooting

q: Is the LTE ACLR requirement always 45 dBc?
a: No. It is 45 dBc or an absolute limit (−13 dBm/MHz for Category A), whichever is less stringent. For a wide carrier at modest per-port power the PSD is low (e.g. ~27 dBm/MHz at 20 MHz), so the absolute limit corresponds to ~40 dBc and that becomes the binding requirement.
tags: tx rct measurements fundamentals troubleshooting

q: Convert 8% EVM to an SNR.
a: EVM ≈ 1/√SNR for noise-like error: SNR = 1/0.08² ≈ 156 ≈ 22 dB. 3.5% (the 256QAM limit) ≈ 29 dB.
tags: tx rct measurements fundamentals troubleshooting

q: Why is EVM also tested with a low-power test model?
a: At low power the converter noise floor, quantisation and fixed spurs are a larger fraction of the signal, so EVM can degrade even though the PA is very linear. The E-TM2 low-power test catches a transmitter that is only clean at full power.
tags: tx rct measurements fundamentals troubleshooting

q: Your ACLR reads 68 dBc on one bench and 58 dBc on another for the same RU. Which is right?
a: Possibly neither is the RU. 68 dBc may be near the analyser's own floor, and 58 may have a wrong attenuation/RBW or no noise correction. Check the instrument ACLR floor with a clean source, optimise mixer level, enable noise correction and use the same averaging and gating. Then compare.
tags: tx rct measurements fundamentals troubleshooting

q: How many 625 Hz units are in one LTE RB, and why 625 Hz?
a: 180 kHz / 625 Hz = 288. 625 Hz is half of the 1.25 kHz PRACH subcarrier spacing, so the register can place the PRACH on the half-subcarrier grid used by the preamble mapping.
tags: rx rct lte fundamentals troubleshooting

q: Derive the FHGW PRACH register for 20 MHz with prach offset 83.
a: (83 − 100/2) × 288 + 852 = 33 × 288 + 852 = 9504 + 852 = 10356. The 852 (532.5 kHz) is half the 6-RB PRACH width minus a 7.5 kHz half-subcarrier shift.
tags: rx rct lte fundamentals troubleshooting

q: You need the PRACH 1.8 MHz lower on the same 5 MHz carrier. What are the new RB offset and register?
a: 1.8 MHz = 10 RBs, so the RB offset goes 14 → 4. The register is linear at 288 per RB: 1284 − 2880 = −1596, which matches (4 − 12.5)·288 + 852. Negative is fine because it is a signed offset from the carrier centre. Update SIB2 prach-FrequencyOffset to match.
tags: rx rct lte fundamentals troubleshooting

q: SIB2 prach-FrequencyOffset and the FHGW register disagree by one RB. Likely cause?
a: A PUCCH configuration difference: NRB_CQI or delta-shift changed the number of edge RBs reserved for PUCCH, and the PRACH/Msg3 start moves by one RB. Recompute the register from the actual SIB2 value.
tags: rx rct lte fundamentals troubleshooting

q: Name the four O-RAN fronthaul planes and what each carries.
a: M-plane: NETCONF/YANG management (config, alarms, PM, software). S-plane: PTP + SyncE timing. C-plane: per-symbol control telling the RU which PRBs/beams/compression to use. U-plane: the frequency-domain IQ samples, DL and UL, including PRACH. C and U run over eCPRI on Ethernet.
tags: common-feature oran architecture protocol call-flow aau troubleshooting

q: Who initiates the M-plane connection, and why?
a: The RU, with NETCONF call-home: after DHCP it opens the SSH/TLS session to the DU/SMO NETCONF client, which then manages it. It solves the discovery problem, since the RU may get a dynamic address and the manager does not know it yet.
tags: common-feature oran architecture protocol call-flow aau troubleshooting

q: What is M-plane supervision for?
a: It is a watchdog. The manager must refresh it periodically. If refreshes stop, the RU assumes it has lost its manager and takes its carriers down in a controlled way, so a radio is never left transmitting with nobody in control.
tags: common-feature oran architecture protocol call-flow aau troubleshooting

q: Why is carrier activation "sync-gated"?
a: The RU must not transmit until its PTP/SyncE timing is locked. Otherwise its symbols would be misaligned with the DU and neighbours (fatal for TDD, and harmful interference in general). Steps like L1-Done/RRH-Ready and PA enable wait for a LOCKED state.
tags: common-feature oran architecture protocol call-flow aau troubleshooting

q: The OAM shows the cell in service but no UE can attach. How do you find the truth?
a: Check bottom-up: RU carrier state in its datastore (ACTIVE?), RU alarms, DU fronthaul counters (U-plane RX from the RU non-zero?) and finally KPI availability counters. A cell state derived from the stack's intent can be green while the RU carriers are disabled.
tags: common-feature oran architecture protocol call-flow aau troubleshooting

q: A carrier stays DISABLED although the RU is up, PTP LOCKED and alarm-free. What do you check?
a: Walk the activation chain for the latest RU session: was the NETCONF client connected, was In-Sync received, and was the per-band frequency config (SET_FREQ → freqConfigd) sent after this connection? Then L1-Done/RRH-Ready, SET_TX_POWER and the UserPlaneConfiguration write, and finally the carrier state callbacks. The first missing step is the break. A classic case is configuration that is not re-sent after an RU reconnect.
tags: common-feature oran troubleshooting call-flow architecture lte aau

q: The BBU logs "failed to receive reply" on the TX-power NETCONF write. Is the BBU at fault?
a: Not necessarily. In the case study the RU's FPGA crashed seconds into applying the config (the unit had lost its identity/calibration after a firmware upgrade), killing the NETCONF agent mid-RPC. The BBU error was the symptom. Check RU alarms and reboot cause at the same timestamp.
tags: common-feature oran troubleshooting call-flow architecture lte aau

q: How do you decide whether an ERROR line in the log is your root cause?
a: Check its frequency over time. Count occurrences per hour across the whole day. If it also appears during known-healthy periods, it is background noise. Only signatures that appear or disappear with the failure are candidates.
tags: common-feature oran troubleshooting call-flow architecture lte aau

q: Why can a cell show "in service" while the RU transmits nothing?
a: The state may be derived from the stack's intent (the cell FSM or MAC cell-start toward its own PHY) rather than the RU's actual carrier state. PHY TX counters on eCPRI are fire-and-forget, so they flow even if the RU is not transmitting. Cross-check RU carrier state, fronthaul RX counters and KPI availability.
tags: common-feature oran troubleshooting call-flow architecture lte aau

q: What regression test proves a "reconfigure on reconnect" fix?
a: Kill or restart the RU M-plane session mid-service (or reboot the RU) and expect, without restarting any BBU pods: reconnect → frequency config re-sent → TX power → carriers READY/ACTIVE → traffic resumes.
tags: common-feature oran troubleshooting call-flow architecture lte aau

q: You edited startup.xml on the RU to change the bandwidth, but after reboot it is back. Why?
a: startup.xml is regenerated on every boot by a startup script from on_the_fly_configs.json. The permanent change is to edit bw_mhz in that JSON (value in Hz), reboot, then verify the generated startup.xml, the running sysrepo datastore and the on-air OBW.
tags: common-feature oran aau troubleshooting lab

q: What does the RU's band-capability advertisement contain and why does it matter?
a: Per band: max total supported bandwidth (e.g. 40 MHz), max and min carrier bandwidth (20 / 5 MHz) and max number of carriers (2). The BBU must configure within these limits. A request outside them is rejected, and that is a common cause of config failures after a planning change.
tags: common-feature oran aau troubleshooting lab

q: After a bandwidth change, what else must you recheck?
a: The BBU cell bandwidth (it must match the RU), PRACH/PUCCH placement and the FHGW PRACH register (they depend on N_RB), the test limits and KPIs that are per-bandwidth (ACLR/SEM/OBW, throughput), and the occupied bandwidth on air.
tags: common-feature oran aau troubleshooting lab

q: What is VTref on a J-Link and what happens if you leave it unconnected?
a: VTref is the target reference voltage input. The probe measures the target's I/O voltage to set its signal levels. It does not power the target. With it unconnected the J-Link sees no target voltage and refuses to connect, which is one reason the board must be powered and booted while flashing.
tags: common-feature aau lab hardware troubleshooting

q: Why must you enter a programming address when flashing a .bin but not a .hex?
a: A .bin is a raw byte image with no address information, so the tool must be told where to place it (0x00000000 for this MCU's flash). Intel-HEX and ELF files carry their load addresses.
tags: common-feature aau lab hardware troubleshooting

q: Name the SWD signals and their J-Link 20-pin positions used here.
a: RESET → 15, SWDIO → 7, GND → 4, SWCLK → 9, VTref → 1. The 5-pin board header is RESET, SWDIO, GND, SWCLK, VTref from left to right.
tags: common-feature aau lab hardware troubleshooting

q: In a 2-carrier test, why is each cell's TX power set 3 dB below the single-carrier value?
a: Both carriers are amplified by the same PA and together must not exceed the RU's rated power. Two equal carriers each get half the power, which is −3 dB. Forgetting this over-drives the PA (ACLR/EVM fail, protection trips) or produces misleading throughput comparisons.
tags: lte-feature lte ue throughput kpi rct

q: Per-UE KPI vs aggregate KPI: what does each prove?
a: The per-UE 1CC KPI proves each carrier still performs like a single carrier while the other is loaded (no cross-carrier degradation). The aggregate "CA or 2CC" KPI (2 × 1CC) proves the RU delivers the combined capacity.
tags: lte-feature lte ue throughput kpi rct

q: Why can cross-carrier CA give more total throughput than two UEs on separate carriers?
a: With CA the scheduler can place each UE's data on whichever carrier has free resources in each TTI (frequency-selective and load-based gains). With fixed one-UE-per-carrier, any idle TTI on one carrier is wasted. The runs showed +11–21% at 5/15/20 MHz.
tags: lte-feature lte ue throughput kpi rct

q: All KPIs pass, but NACK rose to ~4% and UL RSSI rose ~28 dB at 20 MHz. Report it or ignore it?
a: Report it as an observation with data. A higher UL noise/interference floor plus rising NACK/DTX at one bandwidth suggests UL interference, PUCCH/PUSCH decoding or power-control issues that could fail under less ideal radio conditions. It is cheap to investigate now.
tags: lte-feature lte ue throughput kpi rct

q: How would you design a test for a new LTE feature?
a: Understand its trigger, layer, messages and expected counters. Baseline without it. Build a matrix of positive, negative, boundary, stability and regression cases over the relevant axes (band, BW, carriers, CA, UEs, duplex, traffic). Automate it (Robot/pytest) with KPI collection. Judge with explicit per-layer KPI thresholds, and on failure debug layer by layer from the first place the numbers diverge.
tags: lte-feature lte 5g ue kpi automation troubleshooting

q: What does a band-switch data-recovery test measure and what do you capture on failure?
a: The time for user-plane traffic to resume after switching the serving band (e.g. B3 down → B7 up), polled every 30 s up to a 5 min limit, over many iterations, giving success rate and recovery-time statistics. On failure, capture cell L1/L2 readiness and RU TX/RX carrier state, plus UE attach/IP state, to see which hand-off failed.
tags: lte-feature lte 5g ue kpi automation troubleshooting

q: Your throughput KPI "fails" by 6%, but the eNB says it forwarded full rate. How can both be true?
a: They are measured at different layers. eGTP (S1-U) shows what the core offered, while PDCP/MAC show what was delivered over the air. A few-percent gap is normal (headers, retransmissions), and a larger step points at a delivery-layer issue. Always specify the KPI layer.
tags: lte-feature lte 5g ue kpi automation troubleshooting

q: Why is a blocking "wait for iperf to finish" dangerous in a 24-hour test?
a: If one stream dies early (e.g. the UL client exits after a radio blip), nothing checks it until the end, so the result shows hours of zero throughput with no explanation. A watchdog that polls each UE and direction, restarts only the dead stream and records the event keeps the test meaningful and leaves a breadcrumb for RCA.
tags: lte-feature lte 5g ue kpi automation troubleshooting

q: A UE cannot attach. Which order do you check things in?
a: Bottom-up: is the cell on air (RU carriers ACTIVE, PTP locked)? Is the UE camping (SIBs, PLMN, RSRP vs q-RxLevMin)? Is PRACH detected and Msg2/Msg4 sent? Does RRC setup complete? What does NAS say (EMM/5GMM cause)? Did InitialContextSetup succeed and the bearer and GTP-U come up? The first failing step is the layer to debug.
tags: protocol debug troubleshooting lte 5g call-flow

q: What is the difference between HARQ NACK and DTX?
a: NACK: the UE decoded the scheduling grant (PDCCH) but failed to decode the data, and said so. DTX: no feedback was received at all, because the UE missed the PDCCH or the eNB failed to detect the PUCCH/feedback. High DTX points at control-channel or UL-detection problems, and high NACK at data-channel link adaptation or SINR.
tags: protocol debug troubleshooting lte 5g call-flow

q: Throughput is low but the radio report says CQI 15, RI 4, BLER 0. Where do you look?
a: Above the PHY: MAC scheduling and allocated PRBs (other UEs? PRB caps?), RLC window stalls or retransmissions, PDCP discards, and transport/TCP limits (RTT, window, server). Compare throughput at eGTP, MAC and PDCP to see where the drop starts.
tags: protocol debug troubleshooting lte 5g call-flow

q: Why correlate logs from several sources on one timeline?
a: Because each source sees only its own layer. UE traces, eNB logs, pcaps and KPI counters together reveal cause and effect (e.g. an RU fault seconds before a NETCONF error). Check the clocks and time zones first (UTC vs local), or the correlation will mislead.
tags: protocol debug troubleshooting lte 5g call-flow

q: In an S1-side capture, how do you recognise a successful X2 handover?
a: By S1AP PathSwitchRequest from the target eNB followed by PathSwitchRequestAcknowledge from the MME. The handover preparation itself (HandoverRequest/Ack, SN Status Transfer, UE Context Release) happens on X2 and is not in an S1-only capture.
tags: protocol debug handover call-flow lte troubleshooting

q: You see HO attempts in the eNB logs but no Path Switch in the S1 capture. What happened?
a: The handover did not complete from the core's view. The target rejected admission, the UE failed to access the target (RACH), the HO was cancelled, or the UE dropped. Look at X2AP (HandoverPreparationFailure/Cancel) and RRC traces to pin it down.
tags: protocol debug handover call-flow lte troubleshooting

q: How does an S1 handover look different on S1 from an X2 handover?
a: S1 HO uses S1AP HandoverRequired (source → MME), HandoverRequest/Ack (MME ↔ target), HandoverCommand (MME → source), eNB/MME Status Transfer and HandoverNotify. X2 HO shows only Path Switch on S1.
tags: protocol debug handover call-flow lte troubleshooting

q: What is the GTP-U End Marker for?
a: After the path switch the SGW sends an End Marker on the old path, which is forwarded to the target, to mark that no more DL packets will arrive via the source/forwarding path. The target can then deliver forwarded and new-path packets in order and release the forwarding tunnel.
tags: protocol debug handover call-flow lte troubleshooting

q: In a long test, UL throughput went to 0 and stayed there while DL recovered after a radio blip. Why, and how do you fix it?
a: With iPerf the DL receiver on the phone is a UDP server that simply resumes, but the UL sender is a client process on the phone that exits when sendto() fails during the outage. Nothing restarted it because the test blocked in a sequential wait. Fix: a watchdog that polls each UE+direction, restarts only the dead stream after N consecutive zero reads (re-resolving the UE IP), caps restarts, and reports every event.
tags: automation rct ue troubleshooting lte

q: Why debounce with a zero-streak and add ramp-grace / seen-alive rules?
a: Throughput naturally dips for a second or two, and a new stream reads nothing while it starts. Without debounce and grace the watchdog restarts healthy streams, disrupting the test and wasting its restart budget.
tags: automation rct ue troubleshooting lte

q: Your watchdog restarted streams 20 times but only one stall was real. What went wrong?
a: It treated a failed read (SSH/tail error returning None) the same as a confirmed zero. Separate the two: a read error skips the poll, and only a successful ~0 reading counts. Optionally require a corroborating signal such as UL MCS dropping to the floor in the eNB stats.
tags: automation rct ue troubleshooting lte

q: Why must a self-healing test still report every heal?
a: Healing keeps the test running, but the underlying cause (why the UE dropped) is a potential RAN bug. The logged time, stream and outcome let you correlate with eNB/CWS logs afterwards. Silent healing would hide defects.
tags: automation rct ue troubleshooting lte

q: Why run M-plane alarm tests with a live UE and data instead of on an idle RU?
a: Because the product requirement is not only "the alarm appears". It is also "service behaves correctly while faulted and after recovery". Some faults should be transparent to the UE (a thermal warning). Others should take the carrier down and bring it back (a reboot, freerun). You can only prove that with continuity evidence captured during the fault.
tags: automation oran aau netconf sync timing troubleshooting framework python lab

q: Holdover raised after ~3 min, freerun after ~16–18 min. What does that tell you about the test design?
a: Each TC needs its own raise timeout that is longer than the real transition time, and the two sync TCs are naturally sequential: freerun is holdover continued. It also means the sync group costs over half an hour per band, which matters for scheduling (the group took 36:54).
tags: automation oran aau netconf sync timing troubleshooting framework python lab

q: Three TCs failed because the alarm never raised. How do you decide whether it is a product defect?
a: First prove that the injection created the fault condition (read back the temperature, the port state, the register). If the cause was not present, it is a test or injection defect. Only if the cause is confirmed and the RU stays silent is it a product defect. In this run all three were classed as injection-method issues.
tags: automation oran aau netconf sync timing troubleshooting framework python lab

q: What made the suite reusable across both bands and RRHs?
a: Profile switching in run_matrix (b3/b28) plus auto-detection of the PTP interface and the OAM profile per RRH. Nothing band-specific is hard-coded, so --rrh both just loops.
tags: automation oran aau netconf sync timing troubleshooting framework python lab

q: How do you automate a coverage or cell-edge test in the lab?
a: Put a programmable attenuator between the RU and the UE, run continuous traffic, and step the attenuation. At each step, wait for the link to settle, then log the UE RSRP, the DU SNR/CQI/RI/MCS/BLER and the throughput. Finish by returning to 0 dB and checking that throughput recovers. For access coverage, repeat attach N times per level and record the success rate.
tags: automation rx sensitivity prach kpi ue lte lab measurements troubleshooting python

q: B3 reached -110 dBm RACH coverage but B28 only -85 dBm on the same DU. What do you conclude, and why?
a: The shared parts (DU, EPC, UE type, method) are cleared by the B3 control case, so the problem is on the B28 RRH. RACH at the edge is limited by preamble detection in the RU uplink, so a 25 dB gap points to a B28 receive problem. That matched the unit's fault-20 and the conducted sensitivity finding.
tags: automation rx sensitivity prach kpi ue lte lab measurements troubleshooting python

q: DL TCP throughput stalls at cell edge but DL UDP is fine. Why?
a: TCP depends on UL ACKs. A weak uplink loses ACKs, the TCP window collapses and DL stalls, even though the DL radio link is healthy. Test each direction with UDP to separate the radio from the transport.
tags: automation rx sensitivity prach kpi ue lte lab measurements troubleshooting python

q: What should link adaptation look like as the signal fades?
a: A smooth decline: CQI and MCS step down, rank drops from 4 to 1, and BLER stays near its target while outer-loop adaptation corrects. Then a clean recovery when the signal returns. A cliff edge or a stuck low MCS after recovery is a defect.
tags: automation rx sensitivity prach kpi ue lte lab measurements troubleshooting python

q: Why drive throughput tests from a scenario CSV instead of separate test functions?
a: The logic is identical and only the parameters change. A CSV row per scenario means new cases need no code, a command-line filter picks a subset for CI, and each row still reports as its own test ID. It also keeps targets and pass percentages next to the scenario, where reviewers can see them.
tags: automation python framework kpi ue lte measurements

q: Your nightly benchmark is green but took 30 seconds. What happened?
a: Most likely the scenario filter matched zero rows, pytest collected nothing (exit code 5), and CI treated that as success. Fail on an empty selection and treat exit 5 as a failure.
tags: automation python framework kpi ue lte measurements

q: What pass criteria besides "throughput ≥ X % of target" would you add, and why?
a: Datagram error % for UDP (the offered traffic really got through), and duration % (the traffic ran for its whole window, so a dead iPerf cannot pass on a partial average). Log PRB/MCS/RI/SNR/CQI/BLER as well, to explain any miss.
tags: automation python framework kpi ue lte measurements

q: 2CC on this bench is B3+B3. Why not B3+B28?
a: Inter-band CA needs a UE that supports the CA_3-28 band combination. With the available UE, intra-band B3+B3 (15+15 MHz) was the CA configuration that could be exercised.
tags: automation python framework kpi ue lte measurements

q: In a Robot suite, where do keywords come from, and where would you look for the one that decides pass/fail here?
a: From Python libraries (each public method of a *RobotApi class), from resource .robot files, and from the file's own Keywords section. The verdict here is in Verify_B4B7_Throughput_Results in 4G_B4B7_common.robot , which calls the throughput library to parse iPerf and compare with expected × 0.8.
tags: automation framework ue lte kpi python

q: Why wrap each throughput check in Run Keyword And Continue On Failure?
a: So that all four checks (two bands × two directions) are evaluated and reported even if the first fails. You see the complete picture in one run instead of fixing one failure at a time.
tags: automation framework ue lte kpi python

q: The docstring says 180 s and 45/17 Mbps, the Variables say 600 s and 43.75/18.75. Which runs?
a: The Variables. Docstrings and tags are only text. They should be corrected, because readers and CI filters (a 180s tag) are misled by them.
tags: automation framework ue lte kpi python

q: What is risky about Set Suite Variable, and when is it still reasonable?
a: It creates hidden dependencies: resource keywords read variables that were never passed to them, so reordering steps breaks things far from the cause. It is reasonable for suite-wide handles set once in setup (connections, selected UEs and cells). Per-step data should be passed as arguments.
tags: automation framework ue lte kpi python

q: How does this test change the cell bandwidth, and why is that approach good?
a: Through ACS (TR-069): it reads the current parameters, writes only the ones that differ, and reboots only if a reboot-requiring parameter changed, then verifies the carriers. That is idempotent and uses the supported management path, not file edits on the radio.
tags: automation framework ue lte kpi python

q: How would you automatically work out which component crashed during a 48-hour stability run?
a: Scan each new log archive for core files. The core file name (from the kernel core_pattern, e.g. core.%e.%p) contains the crashed thread name. Map that name to a component and pod with a table (MacTxCtlData_C0 → gnb_du_layer2 in the DU pod), write an HTML report and email the team. Then open the core in gdb with the matching symbols for the backtrace.
tags: automation debug troubleshooting architecture 5g nr framework

q: A core file is named core.MacTxCtlData_C0.12345. What do the parts mean?
a: MacTxCtlData_C0 is the name of the thread that crashed (a MAC thread for cell 0 in the DU layer-2 process) and 12345 is the process ID. The name comes from %e in core_pattern, limited to 15 characters.
tags: automation debug troubleshooting architecture 5g nr framework

q: Your triage reported three crashes within two seconds in DU, CU and PHY. How do you read that?
a: Most likely one primary crash and two consequences (peers aborting or being killed by a watchdog after losing their partner). Take the earliest core as the primary, get its backtrace, and check that the others are secondary before filing three bugs.
tags: automation debug troubleshooting architecture 5g nr framework

q: The crash report keeps growing with "No Core in this file" rows for the same archives. Why?
a: Archives without a core are never added to checked.txt, so every poll rescans them. Record every processed archive, not only those with a crash.
tags: automation debug troubleshooting architecture 5g nr framework

q: How do you attach a GPS position to every KPI sample in a drive test?
a: Log NMEA from the GPS receiver and KPIs from the RAN or UE in parallel. Parse GGA for position, VTG/RMC for speed and date, convert everything to UTC, then do a nearest-time join with a tolerance (3 s here). Check how many rows merged, and upload to Elasticsearch with a geo_point field for map views.
tags: automation drive-test python kpi ue measurements lte 5g

q: A merged drive-test file has all the KPIs but empty latitude and longitude. What is the first thing you check?
a: Time alignment. NMEA is UTC and the KPI tool may log local time, so the two never fall within the merge tolerance. Also check that the receiver had a fix (quality ≥ 1) and that the parser recognises $GN… talker IDs.
tags: automation drive-test python kpi ue measurements lte 5g

q: Why cluster stationary GPS points, and how do you pick the radius?
a: So that time spent stopped (traffic lights, junctions) does not dominate per-location statistics, and so repeated visits to one spot are grouped. Pick a radius just above GPS accuracy (5 m by default, since receivers are typically accurate to 2–5 m). Larger radii merge distinct locations.
tags: automation drive-test python kpi ue measurements lte 5g

q: You want to compare RSRP at the same places on two drives. What can go wrong with per-drive cluster IDs?
a: IDs depend on which points exist in each drive, so one extra point can shift the numbering and you end up comparing different places. Cluster the union of both drives once, or use a fixed spatial grid, so an ID means the same location in both.
tags: automation drive-test python kpi ue measurements lte 5g

q: Someone hands you a test name you have never seen. How do you work out what it does and what makes it pass?
a: Find the Test-ID in the setup's tc_cadence.json: test_type gives the analyzer mode, and 5G tests carry their KPIs inline. For 4G, look up the limit and any band override in the kpi_thresholds file. Find the Group that lists the test (band/BW/frequency/TM) and the Cadence that includes that group. Then apply cable loss and the verdict direction.
tags: automation rct framework kpi measurements reference python

q: Why can one 5G Test-ID produce several verdicts?
a: Because the modulation-analysis measurement returns several quantities at once. Its KPI block has output power (window), EVM (max %), frequency error (± Hz) and TAE (max ns), and each is judged separately.
tags: automation rct framework kpi measurements reference python

q: ACLR is 54 dBc in one place and 55 dBc in another. Which is right?
a: Both. They come from different setups and files: 54 with 1 dB tolerance inline in a 5G Test-ID, 55 with 0.8 or 0 dB tolerance in 4G threshold files, and 52 for some dual-band overrides. The applicable limit is the one resolved for that setup, band and dual-band step.
tags: automation rct framework kpi measurements reference python

q: What is MARGINAL_RESULT and how is it computed for sensitivity?
a: It is the Pass(Tolerance) verdict. Sensitivity is lower-is-better: pass if the RU input power at the 5 % BLER crossing is ≤ KPI, marginal if ≤ KPI + tolerance (e.g. 1.0 dB), otherwise fail.
tags: automation rct framework kpi measurements reference python

q: You changed a value in setup.json and the test ignored it. Why?
a: The configuration layers merge in order and later layers win. A test_inputs file (or a cadence-level override) probably defines the same key. Search every layer for the key.
tags: automation rct framework kpi measurements reference python

q: How is an integration feature test organised in this suite?
a: One folder per feature epic, one .robot file per group of test-case IDs, a feature-level common.robot with shared keywords, and a data-driven test table where each TCM row calls the same flow keyword with different arguments. The flow is: configure, restart, verify health, start capture and traffic, trigger, stop, assert IEs, assert counters, assert throughput.
tags: automation framework python lab handover

q: How does the framework assert a protocol IE?
a: It captures control-plane traffic on the node, then a keyword applies a Wireshark display filter (with a product Lua post-dissector) and compares a named field with the expected value, returning the packet or raising NO_PACKETS / FOUND_NOT_EQUAL. Negative checks wrap the same keyword in Run Keyword And Expect Error.
tags: automation framework python lab handover

q: What does run_robot.py add on top of plain robot?
a: Loops (--repeat), automatic re-runs of failed tests (rerunfailed:N), merged reports via rebot, log retention, report title and build number, variables such as the setup config path, technology and test mode, and optional Elasticsearch upload.
tags: automation framework python lab handover

q: Walk through the CI flow for a nightly integration run.
a: Jenkins locks a physical setup by label, clones the test repo, downloads the product build from Artifactory by commit, installs it, runs the robot command with the setup's config path substituted, then archives XML/HTML/logs, publishes them with the Robot plugin and e-mails the result.
tags: automation framework python lab handover

q: What would you improve first in this framework?
a: Replace fixed sleeps with state polling (and record recovery times), verify that injected faults really happened, move hard-coded ARFCNs and pod names into setup config, and key multi-UE assertions on UE identifiers. Also add the missing feature areas (CMAS/ETWS, CHO).
tags: automation framework python lab handover

q: Write the relation between the DU send window and the RU receive window in the downlink.
a: T1a_max_up = T2a_max_up + T12_min and T1a_min_up = T2a_min_up + T12_max. The earliest send uses the minimum delay, so a fast packet is not early. The latest send uses the maximum delay, so a slow packet is not late. The DU window is therefore narrower than the RU window by T12_max − T12_min.
tags: common-feature oran fronthaul timing sync architecture netconf troubleshooting evm reference

q: And in the uplink?
a: Ta4_min = Ta3_min + T34_min and Ta4_max = Ta3_max + T34_max. The DU must accept everything the RU can send across the full delay range, so its window is wider by the UL delay spread.
tags: common-feature oran fronthaul timing sync architecture netconf troubleshooting evm reference

q: EVM fails on a few symbols per slot while channel power and ACLR are fine on an O-RAN RU. What do you suspect?
a: Late DL U-plane packets. The RU zero-fills or drops symbols whose IQ missed the T2a window. I would read rx-window-stats (RX_LATE / RX_EARLY), confirm PTP lock on both ends, and check whether the DU L1 real-time cores are shared or overloaded.
tags: common-feature oran fronthaul timing sync architecture netconf troubleshooting evm reference

q: Why does fronthaul jitter matter more than average latency?
a: A constant delay can be absorbed by moving the DU window earlier. Variation (T12_max − T12_min) shrinks the DU send window directly, and once it exceeds the RU buffer depth (T2a_max_up − T2a_min_up) no valid send time exists.
tags: common-feature oran fronthaul timing sync architecture netconf troubleshooting evm reference

q: Where does a DU learn the RU's windows?
a: From the RU delay profile in the o-ran-delay-management YANG module over the M-plane (t2a-min-up, t2a-max-up, ta3-min, ta3-max, the C-plane values and tcp-adv-dl). The transport delays T12/T34 can be configured into the RU in the same module.
tags: common-feature oran fronthaul timing sync architecture netconf troubleshooting evm reference

q: An AAU shows fault 12 "Critical file not found" on its b41 carriers only. What do you check?
a: Which file: the alarm source names it. In GRDEV-9046 it was tx_calibration_eeprom.json, never generated because start_transmission.sh chose the calibration route by matching hard-coded model names and the b41 sub-variant was missing. It appeared on the release branch only, which pointed at packaging, not the unit. The practical impact is an uncalibrated TX carrier, so output power cannot be certified.
tags: common-feature oran aau troubleshooting debug hardware rffe sync netconf reference

q: Fault 17 and then fault 18 appear some minutes apart. What happened?
a: The RU lost all sync inputs and went into holdover (17). When holdover could no longer keep the time within limits it declared freerun (18) and stopped RF. In our CMN_009/010 tests the gaps were about 3 min and 16–18 min after the PTP master port was disabled.
tags: common-feature oran aau troubleshooting debug hardware rffe sync netconf reference

q: Fault 15 "Unit out of order" is in the log 38 times after a conformance run. Is the unit broken?
a: Not necessarily. In our case every occurrence lined up with the framework tearing carriers down to reconfigure frequency or E-TM: the TRX chains go DISABLED, the LED manager raises unit-out-of-order, then the carriers come back. Count the alarms against reconfiguration events before filing a defect.
tags: common-feature oran aau troubleshooting debug hardware rffe sync netconf reference

q: What is the difference between fault-ids 20 and 1000+?
a: IDs 1–41 are the O-RAN common alarms with a defined meaning (20 = RX out of order). 1000–65535 is the vendor-specific range, so an ID such as 2003 has only the meaning the vendor documents.
tags: common-feature oran aau troubleshooting debug hardware rffe sync netconf reference

q: An RU's EPE CSV gives O-RAN-B1 = 176 W, but the four RFFEs of band 1 only add up to 152 W. Is the file wrong?
a: No. The band total also includes a share of the RFFE-CONTROLLER (the 12 V FHGW + mid-board rail): half of 47.6 W on a two-band flavour, all of it on the single-band B41 flavour. Flavour power is B1 + B2, which equals the sum of all RFFEs plus CONTROLLER0 once.
tags: common-feature oran measurements power efficiency aau rffe netconf kpi troubleshooting

q: Your summed AAU power comes out ~120 W higher than get-PSU. What is the first thing you check?
a: Double counting of RFFE-CONTROLLER1. It mirrors CONTROLLER0 for V/I/P, and its temperature reads 0. Summing both adds 35–50 W per flavour. After that, check for mixed builds and for summing min/max instead of avg.
tags: common-feature oran measurements power efficiency aau rffe netconf kpi troubleshooting

q: A PM file shows 6553.5 V and -1310.71 W. What happened and how should automation treat it?
a: 0xFFFF × 0.1 is a failed sensor read (a sentinel), not a measurement. Mark the minute or the whole flavour as invalid, exclude it and report the gap. Never coerce it to 0 W: that would look like a huge energy saving.
tags: common-feature oran measurements power efficiency aau rffe netconf kpi troubleshooting

q: Why must the lab supply and get-PSU be binned on hh:mm:00 boundaries?
a: O-RAN aligns PM measurement intervals to midnight (seconds mod interval = 0), so each 60-s EPE block runs from :00 to :00. If another source uses free-running minutes from when the script started, you compare different time windows. During warm-up or load changes that shows up as fake error.
tags: common-feature oran measurements power efficiency aau rffe netconf kpi troubleshooting

q: PM and the lab DC supply differ by a near-constant ~50 W at light load. Error or boundary?
a: Mostly boundary. The CSV sums rail outputs (RFFE rails + 12 V controller rail) as V×I. The lab supply sees the chassis input, including PSU conversion loss, the common board and cabling. A constant offset points to a boundary difference. An error that grows with load points to the efficiency model, which is what GRDEV-9526 calibrated.
tags: common-feature oran measurements power efficiency aau rffe netconf kpi troubleshooting

q: Name the O-RAN M-plane energy-saving techniques and the one that also stops the M-plane.
a: Carrier deactivation (and carrier SLEEP), RF channel switch-off via C-plane or M-plane TRX control, data-layer control, Advanced Sleep Modes, deep hibernate and maximum output power control. Deep hibernate is the one that stops C/U/S and then the M-plane. The O-RU restarts when hibernate-time expires, with restart-cause DEEP-HIBERNATE-RESTART.
tags: common-feature oran power efficiency netconf architecture aau optimization standards

q: The DU sends deep-hibernate while one carrier is still active. What must the O-RU do?
a: Reject the RPC and include the reason in the error message. All tx and rx array-carriers must be deactivated first. This is a good negative test case.
tags: common-feature oran power efficiency netconf architecture aau optimization standards

q: How is PW uSleep different from O-RAN Advanced Sleep Modes?
a: ASM is commanded by the DU over the C-plane, using advertised sleep types and wake-up durations, and works at array or processing level. uSleep is decided autonomously inside the RU FPGA per empty OFDM symbol, and gates the PA enable line. It is transparent to the DU and not part of any O-RAN interface.
tags: common-feature oran power efficiency netconf architecture aau optimization standards

q: What is the standard counterpart of Reduced Output Power, and what extra obligation does it place on the DU?
a: MAX-POWER-CONTROL, per tx-array index or per carrier reduction in dB. The DU must restrict scheduled PRBs so the IQ level stays below the reduced maximum. It must lower power before increasing the reduction, and only raise power after the max-power-level-used notification confirms a smaller reduction.
tags: common-feature oran power efficiency netconf architecture aau optimization standards

q: Why might carrier re-activation be slow after an energy-saving period, and how do you guarantee it is instant?
a: With energy-saving-enabled=true and no active carrier the O-RU may go SLEEPING and stop the S-plane. Re-activation then waits for sync. Setting energy-saving-enabled=false keeps the O-RU AWAKE and ready to activate immediately.
tags: common-feature oran power efficiency netconf architecture aau optimization standards

q: NETCONF shows the new bandwidth, but UEs stop attaching after an on-the-fly BW change. Where do you look?
a: Below the datastore: the value the signal path actually uses. In GRDEV-8976 the DFE channel filter stayed at 10 MHz while the carrier was 15 MHz, so the edge PRBs where SIB1 is scheduled were stripped and SIB1 failed CRC. The filter reload only ran on a centre-frequency change, and after reset it was sized from the personality default.
tags: common-feature aau oran troubleshooting debug hardware rffe calibration netconf

q: A critical alarm appears on every bring-up with one software branch but not another. What does that tell you?
a: The fault follows the software, not the hardware: packaging or a regression. In GRDEV-9046 a start-up script whitelisted model names and missed the b41 sub-variant, so the TX calibration file was never generated.
tags: common-feature aau oran troubleshooting debug hardware rffe calibration netconf

q: All four RFFEs report over-current at every boot. Hardware failure?
a: Very unlikely: four simultaneous failures at every power-up point to a shared cause. In GRDEV-8838 it was mid-board firmware supervision (read through I2C status registers) raising a false over-current, fixed in a later firmware release.
tags: common-feature aau oran troubleshooting debug hardware rffe calibration netconf

q: How do you find bugs in the test framework itself?
a: Compare framework output with the instrument screen on a few points of every new measurement. That is how the SEM wrong-segment index, the shifted dynamic-range column and the never-written PRACH re-offset were found; dry runs had passed.
tags: common-feature aau oran troubleshooting debug hardware rffe calibration netconf

q: Why do modern sites rarely use TMAs?
a: The RRU or AAU sits within a few metres of the antenna, so less than about 1 dB of loss precedes the receiver. A TMA recovers feeder loss on the uplink; with no long feeder there is little to recover, and it adds a failure point and DL insertion loss.
tags: common-feature hardware antenna aau power fundamentals reference

q: How is a TMA powered, and how do you know it is working?
a: The radio or a bias-tee puts DC (typically 7–30 V) on the coax. The radio watches the DC current and raises a TMA alarm if it leaves the expected window, and the TMA falls back to bypass. The idle UL RSSI also rises by roughly the TMA gain, which must be entered in the configuration.
tags: common-feature hardware antenna aau power fundamentals reference

q: Size the battery for a 3.6 kW site that needs 4 hours of backup.
a: 3.6 kW at 48 V is 75 A. 3600 × 4 / (48 × 0.8) ≈ 375 Ah, so fit 400 Ah (two strings of 200 Ah). Also size the rectifiers for load plus recharge current (≈115 A) with one spare module, and remember that cold batteries deliver less capacity.
tags: common-feature hardware antenna aau power fundamentals reference

q: A tower radio reboots only during mains failures. Why?
a: Voltage drop. On battery the bus falls towards 44–46 V, and the IR drop in a long, thin DC cable takes the radio below its minimum input voltage. Check the cable cross-section against the load current and length; the fix is a thicker cable or a DC booster.
tags: common-feature hardware antenna aau power fundamentals reference

q: Why is site earthing tested in the dry season?
a: Soil resistivity is highest when dry, so that is the worst case. A value that meets the limit only after rain will fail when it matters.
tags: common-feature hardware antenna aau power fundamentals reference

q: Convert VSWR 1.5 to return loss. Is it good?
a: Γ = 0.5/2.5 = 0.2, so RL ≈ 14 dB, with 4 % of the power reflected and 0.18 dB mismatch loss. The loss is small, but for a new installation it is only marginal. Many operators want RL ≥ 17–18 dB (VSWR ≈1.3) for the antenna line.
tags: common-feature measurements antenna hardware instruments troubleshooting fronthaul

q: A sweep from the bottom of a 60 m feeder passes, but the site drops calls in rain. What next?
a: Run DTF with the correct velocity factor and cable loss, and compare it with the baseline. Feeder attenuation masks a bad joint at the top in the aggregate RL. Check UL noise per branch in wet and dry conditions, and do a PIM test. Water in a top connector is the usual cause.
tags: common-feature measurements antenna hardware instruments troubleshooting fronthaul

q: Why must the velocity factor be right?
a: DTF converts round-trip time to distance using the propagation speed in the cable. A 10 % error puts you metres away from the real fault on a tall tower.
tags: common-feature measurements antenna hardware instruments troubleshooting fronthaul

q: Rx optical power on a fronthaul link is −13.8 dBm with an LR SFP. Pass?
a: It is within the window but only about 0.6 dB above the ≈−14.4 dBm sensitivity, so there is no margin. Clean and inspect the connectors, check for tight bends and bad splices with the OTDR, and aim for several dB of margin before accepting.
tags: common-feature measurements antenna hardware instruments troubleshooting fronthaul

q: What proves a microwave hop is correctly aligned?
a: RSL within a couple of dB of the planned value on both ends (not a side lobe, which reads 20 dB or more lower), expected cross-polar discrimination, and an error-free service test at the planned capacity.
tags: common-feature measurements antenna hardware instruments troubleshooting fronthaul

q: SCTP to the MME is ESTABLISHED but S1 Setup keeps failing. Where do you look?
a: At the S1 Setup Failure cause and the identities it carries. The PLMN and TAC must be configured on the MME, and the eNB ID must be allowed and unique. Transport is already fine because SCTP is up.
tags: common-feature call-flow architecture lte 5g nr sync reference troubleshooting

q: Which ports would you open on a firewall for X2 and Xn?
a: SCTP 36422 for X2AP and SCTP 38422 for XnAP, plus UDP 2152 for GTP-U data forwarding. 36412 (S1AP) and 38412 (NGAP) are the core-facing ports that people copy by mistake.
tags: common-feature call-flow architecture lte 5g nr sync reference troubleshooting

q: Convert EARFCN 1650 and NR-ARFCN 636000 to frequencies.
tags: common-feature call-flow architecture lte 5g nr sync reference troubleshooting

q: Why is NTP not enough to synchronise a TDD cell?
a: NTP delivers time of day with millisecond-level accuracy over the network, and no frequency reference. TDD needs ±1.5 µs phase alignment and ±0.05 ppm frequency, which require GNSS or PTP with suitable network support (plus SyncE if used).
tags: common-feature call-flow architecture lte 5g nr sync reference troubleshooting

q: Explain PCI confusion with an example.
a: Cell A has two neighbours, B and C, which both use PCI 150. When a UE reports PCI 150, cell A cannot tell which one is meant and may prepare the handover towards the wrong cell. The fix is to re-plan one of the two PCIs.
tags: common-feature call-flow architecture lte 5g nr sync reference troubleshooting

q: What is the difference between SCFT and SSV?
a: SCFT tests each cell's functions next to the site in good RF: attach, data, voice, SMS, intra-site handover. SSV is a drive test around the site that checks the footprint per sector, PCI versus azimuth and handovers to real neighbours. It catches crossed feeders and overshooting, which SCFT cannot see.
tags: common-feature kpi measurements call-flow drive-test reference lte 5g

q: What is the difference between PAC and FAC?
a: Provisional acceptance lets the site carry commercial traffic while minor punch items stay open. Final acceptance comes after a KPI observation period, once every item and document is closed. It is usually tied to payment and the start of the warranty.
tags: common-feature kpi measurements call-flow drive-test reference lte 5g

q: The drive test shows sector B's PCI in sector C's direction. What happened, and how do you prove the fix?
a: Crossed feeders or fibres, or a wrong cell-to-radio mapping in the configuration. Correct the cabling or mapping, then repeat the PCI-versus-azimuth drive and the per-branch RSSI check, and attach the new results to the punch-list item.
tags: common-feature kpi measurements call-flow drive-test reference lte 5g

q: How do you test alarm integration during commissioning?
a: Create real conditions: pull a fronthaul fibre, open the cabinet door, switch mains off so the site runs on battery. Confirm that each alarm reaches the NMS with the correct severity, object and timestamp, and that it clears when the condition is removed.
tags: common-feature kpi measurements call-flow drive-test reference lte 5g

q: Your new site misses its drop-rate target, but its radio and transport are clean. What next?
a: Break the drops down by cause and by neighbour relation. Drops often cluster on handovers to one neighbour (missing relation, PCI conflict, the neighbour's tilt). Fix it or document it as a cluster issue, so the site is not rejected for a problem it did not cause.
tags: common-feature kpi measurements call-flow drive-test reference lte 5g

q: The NOC reports 40 alarms on a site at once. How do you start?
a: Sort by time and by layer. Take the earliest alarm in the lowest layer (power, then transport, then sync), fix that and watch whether the others clear. Most of the list is usually consequences.
tags: common-feature troubleshooting debug hardware power sync antenna

q: A VSWR alarm appears every morning and clears by midday. Likely cause?
a: A connector or jumper that lets in moisture, or whose contact changes with temperature: dew at night, drying and expansion during the day. Check the weatherproofing and compare DTF with the acceptance trace to find the joint.
tags: common-feature troubleshooting debug hardware power sync antenna

q: GNSS is lost but the cells are still on air. Is that OK?
a: Only for a while. The clock is in holdover and stays within limits for a vendor-dependent time. Fix the GNSS before holdover expires, because TDD cells normally stop transmitting once phase accuracy can no longer be guaranteed.
tags: common-feature troubleshooting debug hardware power sync antenna

q: Ping to the MME works but the S1 alarm stays. What else do you check?
a: The SCTP association (a firewall may pass ICMP but block SCTP 36412), the peer addresses configured on both ends, and the S1 Setup result. A PLMN or TAC mismatch fails at the application layer even when transport is fine.
tags: common-feature troubleshooting debug hardware power sync antenna

q: Why is preventive maintenance worth the truck roll?
a: Most site outages come from slow degradation: ageing batteries, drying weatherproofing, clogged filters, drifting optical levels. Finding them on a planned visit is much cheaper than an outage, and trend data (VSWR, optical Rx, battery backup time) shows which sites to visit first.
tags: common-feature troubleshooting debug hardware power sync antenna

q: What is the minimum you check before starting L1/L2 on a freshly flashed FHGW?
a: Model string read back, firmware version in rfsoc_fru_detail, PTP "synchronized" with small offsets, the startup.xml DU MAC matching the DU port, the re-offset for the BW, and carriers active per antenna (sysrepocfg and md.l). Only then start l1 and l2 and verify with power-monitor.
tags: rct lab hardware oran fronthaul netconf sync prach debug troubleshooting

q: How do you compute the re-offset for a 15 MHz carrier without CA?
tags: rct lab hardware oran fronthaul netconf sync prach debug troubleshooting

q: Why are nonRtCores written as "1,33" on a 32-core server?
a: The second number is the hyper-thread sibling of the first (core + N). The same pattern gives l1RtCores 5,6,37,38. Check /opt/cpualloc.json so the L1 real-time cores are not already taken by another pod.
tags: rct lab hardware oran fronthaul netconf sync prach debug troubleshooting

q: Carriers show active and L1/L2 run, but power-monitor reads nothing. Where do you look?
a: Fronthaul addressing first: DU MAC in startup.xml, cuMac/ruMac in oammgrconfig.xml, and the physical port in vfs-data.json. Then PhyStartMode (7 for split 7.2), the library swap for flex-run, and the fhgw.log greps for TRX Carrier / DAC Channel / Fault lines.
tags: rct lab hardware oran fronthaul netconf sync prach debug troubleshooting

q: What is the difference between dBi and dBd, and between EIRP and ERP?
a: dBi is gain relative to an isotropic radiator. dBd is relative to a half-wave dipole, which has 2.15 dBi. So dBi = dBd + 2.15 and ERP = EIRP − 2.15 dB.
tags: fundamentals propagation antenna optimization lte 5g

q: Electrical versus mechanical tilt — which do you prefer and why?
a: Electrical tilt, because it tilts the whole pattern uniformly and keeps the horizontal footprint. It can also be changed remotely through RET/AISG. Mechanical tilt dips only the boresight, widens the horizontal pattern and raises the back lobe.
tags: fundamentals propagation antenna optimization lte 5g

q: How do you choose an initial downtilt?
a: Tilt ≈ atan(Δh/d_edge) + θV/2 puts the upper −3 dB edge on the cell edge. For a 30 m mast, 1 km edge and 7° vertical beamwidth that is about 5°. Then refine it with terrain, planning-tool predictions and a drive test.
tags: fundamentals propagation antenna optimization lte 5g

q: A panel has 65° × 7° beamwidth. Roughly what gain do you expect?
a: The ideal figure is 41 253/(65×7) ≈ 91, or 19.6 dBi. Real panels have side lobes and losses, so expect about 17–18 dBi.
tags: fundamentals propagation antenna optimization lte 5g

q: Why are cellular panels ±45° dual-slant?
a: Two orthogonal polarisations in one radome give two uncorrelated branches for diversity or 2-layer MIMO without a second antenna. ±45° also treats horizontal and vertical components of the scattered field equally.
tags: fundamentals propagation antenna optimization lte 5g

q: Why does a 700/800 MHz layer cover so much better than 2.6 or 3.5 GHz?
a: FSPL is 20·log(f), so 800 → 3500 MHz already costs about 13 dB. Diffraction and penetration are also better at low frequency, and empirical models (Hata/COST-231, 38.901) add more loss at higher f. Together that is often 15–25 dB, which is a big change in cell radius.
tags: fundamentals propagation lte 5g optimization drive-test

q: When do you use Okumura-Hata, COST-231 Hata and 3GPP TR 38.901?
a: Hata covers 150–1500 MHz macro cells from 1 to 20 km. COST-231 Hata extends it to 1500–2000 MHz, with +3 dB for dense urban. 38.901 covers 0.5–100 GHz with UMa/UMi/RMa/InH and LOS probability, so it is used for 5G mid-band and mmWave.
tags: fundamentals propagation lte 5g optimization drive-test

q: What fade margin gives 95 % location probability with 8 dB shadowing?
a: FM = z·σ = 1.645 × 8 ≈ 13.2 dB at the cell edge. The area coverage probability will be higher than 95 %.
tags: fundamentals propagation lte 5g optimization drive-test

q: What is the Fresnel zone and how much must be clear?
a: It is the ellipsoid around the LOS path where the main energy travels. F₁ (m) = 17.32·√(d₁d₂/(f·d)) with d in km and f in GHz. Keep at least 60 % of F₁ clear; otherwise diffraction loss appears even with visual line of sight.
tags: fundamentals propagation lte 5g optimization drive-test

q: How far is the radio horizon from a 30 m mast to a handset?
a: About 4.12·(√30 + √1.5) ≈ 27.6 km with the standard k = 4/3 atmosphere.
tags: fundamentals propagation lte 5g optimization drive-test

q: What is the reuse distance for a 7-cell cluster, and why don't LTE and NR use it?
a: D = R·√(3N) = √21·R ≈ 4.58R, which gives an S/I of about 18.7 dB. LTE and NR use reuse-1 for maximum spectral efficiency. They cope with low edge SINR through link adaptation, HARQ, scheduling, ICIC and PCI planning.
tags: fundamentals propagation optimization kpi lte 5g reference

q: How many Erlangs can 10 channels carry at 2 % blocking?
a: About 5.08 Erl (51 % utilisation). 30 channels carry about 21.9 Erl (73 %). This is trunking efficiency: bigger pools are more efficient.
tags: fundamentals propagation optimization kpi lte 5g reference

q: What goes wrong if a tracking area is too big or too small?
a: Too big: paging load on every cell and on the core rises. Too small: TAU/registration storms at the borders. Size it from paging and TAU counters, and keep borders away from busy roads and railways.
tags: fundamentals propagation optimization kpi lte 5g reference

q: What does Shannon say about a 20 MHz carrier at 20 dB SNR?
a: C = 20 MHz × log₂(101) ≈ 133 Mbit/s per spatial stream. It is the upper bound that the MCS table approaches; MIMO layers multiply it.
tags: fundamentals propagation optimization kpi lte 5g reference

q: Why does sectorisation increase capacity?
a: Each directional sector sees fewer co-channel interferers, and each sector is a separate cell reusing the spectrum. Three sectors roughly triple site capacity without new spectrum, at the cost of more handovers and overlap.
tags: fundamentals propagation optimization kpi lte 5g reference

q: A multi-band AAU at 0 % allocation draws almost as much as at 50 %. Why, and why does it matter for uSleep?
a: At 0 % allocation LTE still sends CRS in several symbols of every subframe, plus PDCCH and the sync and broadcast channels. The PA stays biased and switched on all the time. In the reference runs a mid-band PA drew ~37 W at 0 % against ~78 W at 100 %. That idle burn is the headroom uSleep targets: gate the PA during the all-zero symbols.
tags: rct tx measurements aau power efficiency lab hardware kpi

q: Your lab supply reads 206 W with nothing on air, but the internal PSU telemetry sums to 161 W. Which is right?
a: Both are right. They measure at different points. The lab supply includes cabling, PSU conversion and common-board losses (about 45 W here), while the internal rails do not. Compare increments within one source: adding B8 at 0 % added +44 W on both, and B8 at 100 % added +91 W on both. Never subtract a PM or internal "on" value from a lab "off" value.
tags: rct tx measurements aau power efficiency lab hardware kpi

q: A summary sheet says "B41 at 0 % load = 2 W PA rail". What would you check?
a: Whether B41 actually radiated during the averaging window. Look at the per-RFFE PM currents and the lab-supply trace for a step. In the archive, B41 radiated for only the first ~16 minutes of that run (≈100 W) and then stopped. The lab supply fell by the same ~99 W. The 2 W figure is a second-half average taken after TX stopped.
tags: rct tx measurements aau power efficiency lab hardware kpi

q: Why does the analysis script refuse to zero-fill missing samples?
a: A missing sample filled with 0 W pulls the mean down. In an on-versus-off comparison that looks like a power saving that never happened. The script aligns streams on a common grid and leaves gaps as gaps. It also drops the unused RFFE4-7 on single-band flavours, whose leakage readings would otherwise add noise.
tags: rct tx measurements aau power efficiency lab hardware kpi

q: How big is thermal drift compared with a plausible uSleep saving?
a: At full load on all flavours the lab supply rose ~170 W (1266 → 1439 W) in one hour as the PAs heated. On mid-band alone it was ~46 W in 20 minutes. That is as large as, or larger than, the saving you are trying to measure. So compare on and off at thermal steady state, cool down between runs, and alternate the order.
tags: rct tx measurements aau power efficiency lab hardware kpi

q: A campaign reports 236 of 248 points passing. Is the product 95 % good?
a: That is the wrong way to read it. Look at where the 12 non-passes sit. Here all 2 fails and all 10 untested points were on B28 RX, while B3, B1 and B41 were fully clean on the same kind of hardware. The real statement is that one band's receive path has a hardware problem and everything else conforms.
tags: rct measurements tx rx sensitivity aau lte lab troubleshooting standards

q: B28 sensitivity is 4 dB short. How do you prove it is the radio and not your bench?
a: Use a control on the same setup: B3 on the same unit, DU, PHY build, instrument and calibrated reference plane passed by 2–5 dB. Rule out the instrument, cabling, build, RX gain config and sync one by one. Then corroborate with an independent test: PRACH missed detection was worse on B28 at a stronger input. Finally check with manual injection that the path is alive, which shows it is a deficit and not a dead path.
tags: rct measurements tx rx sensitivity aau lte lab troubleshooting standards

q: Why is a pass on the FHGW-in-a-box rig not enough for customer sign-off?
a: The rig has no PA and no antenna. It proves the fronthaul, PHY and digital chain, but not the RF front end the customer receives. The same test list has to run on the full AAU, on every antenna, per customer configuration. The rig remains the fast regression loop.
tags: rct measurements tx rx sensitivity aau lte lab troubleshooting standards

q: Every configuration fails dynamic range by a similar amount. What do you suspect first?
a: The measurement. A uniform miss across different bands, bandwidths and units suggests a common cause. Here the single-RB minimum-power reading sat about 1 dB high, which shrinks the computed range on every run. Re-measure the low-power point (analyser noise floor, attenuation, averaging) before blaming the hardware.
tags: rct measurements tx rx sensitivity aau lte lab troubleshooting standards

q: What is the difference between "not tested" and "not executed" in a campaign report?
a: "Not tested" points are in the counted scope but were not run. Here the unit was returned mid-campaign, so they appear in the denominator. "Not executed" means a whole configuration never started. Its workbook sheets are empty templates, so it is excluded from the count and carried forward. Mixing the two either inflates the pass rate or hides open work.
tags: rct measurements tx rx sensitivity aau lte lab troubleshooting standards

q: You reduce carrier power by 10 dB and ACLR gets worse. Is the radio broken?
a: Not necessarily. On a DPD-linearised PA this is expected unless DPD is retrained. The coefficients were learned at rated power, so at back-off the PA's AM-AM/AM-PM and memory behaviour no longer match the model. Fixed noise floors also matter more at low output. Here ACLR fell by up to 6.2 dB but stayed 6.2 dB or more inside 44.2 dB, so it was recorded as a characteristic.
tags: rct tx power aclr measurements efficiency automation aau lte

q: Commanded −10 dB, achieved −9.17 dB. How do you grade it, and what would you look at next?
a: Grade the achieved step against the commanded one: the error is +0.83 dB, inside ±1.5 dB, so it passes. Next, note that the error grows with step size and is always positive, and that B1 read +1.74/+1.57 at −10 dB. That suggests a per-band gain-law slope below 1 dB per dB. Characterise it in 1 dB steps per band, because an operator configuring −10 dB expects −10 dB.
tags: rct tx power aclr measurements efficiency automation aau lte

q: Your PAPR at 0 dB reads 8.99 dB, but 11.4 dB at −3 and −10 dB. Explain it.
a: Check the CCDF settings. The 0 dB value came from the 0.0001 % tail statistic rather than a full-count capture. At full count it read about 11.4 dB, like the others. Always report PAPR with its probability level and sample count.
tags: rct tx power aclr measurements efficiency automation aau lte

q: Why must the gain change be done inside an atomic carrier cycle?
a: The gain write needs the carrier deactivated, then written, then reactivated. If the automation is interrupted between those steps (timeout, exception or a parallel step), the carrier can be left down or at an unknown gain. The next measurement then grades the wrong state. Making the cycle atomic, so it always completes or rolls back, removes that failure mode.
tags: rct tx power aclr measurements efficiency automation aau lte

q: Why calibrate RSSI only on the −80…−50 dBm plateau?
a: Below about −100 dBm the reading flattens at the noise floor, and near −46…−40 dBm it bends into the knee. In both regions the readout does not track the input one-for-one. The old method sampled the knee and read high by up to 0.58 dB, with a non-constant bias. Averaging 120–480 plateau rows gives a stable, linear offset.
tags: rct rssi rx calibration measurements aau framework debug troubleshooting

q: The radio stores one RSSI correction per band, but each frequency wants a different one. Which value do you store?
a: The minimax value, the middle of the measured spread, so the worst error anywhere in the band is half the spread. For B1 the spread was 2.10 dB, so storing −34.41 gives a worst case of 1.09 dB, inside ±2 dB. Storing either extreme gives 2.11 dB and fails.
tags: rct rssi rx calibration measurements aau framework debug troubleshooting

q: B8 fails ±2 dB whatever value you store. What are your options?
a: Half of B8's ≈4.5 dB spread already exceeds 2 dB, so one coefficient cannot work. Option 1: re-centre to −26.64, which still fails by 0.25 dB. Option 2: exclude the 897.5 MHz dip from the supported range, a product decision. Option 3: add a per-channel correction indexed by frequency, a firmware change good to under 0.5 dB. Pick based on the customer's real B8 channels.
tags: rct rssi rx calibration measurements aau framework debug troubleshooting

q: RSSI moved by exactly the DSA change, but sensitivity did not move at all. What does that tell you?
a: The receive path is healthy and only the reporting offset is wrong. adc_dbfs_adj tracks the DSA one-for-one and never touches the signal. B8's offset had been characterised at DSA 0 but shipped at DSA 10, which gave an ~11 dB readout error. The fix is to recalibrate at the shipped DSA and to gate every apply on a DSA read-back.
tags: rct rssi rx calibration measurements aau framework debug troubleshooting

q: How do you know a calibration is understood and not just tuned until it passed?
a: Predict the post-change error from the plateau model, apply the value, re-run the full sweep and compare. Here prediction and hardware agreed within 0.10 dB at all seven B1/B3 points. Guard the apply step too: a DSA gate, a stale-premise check, and a live read-back.
tags: rct rssi rx calibration measurements aau framework debug troubleshooting

q: What is the difference between a smoke test and full RCT conformance?
a: A smoke test is breadth-first and fast: two TX measurements (ACLR, EVM) on every unit, flavour and antenna, to prove nothing is dead or grossly wrong. Full RCT is depth-first: the whole TS 36.141 TX and RX suite per customer configuration. Smoke gates the start of deeper testing. It cannot replace it, because for example it has no RX coverage.
tags: rct tx aclr evm measurements aau hardware lte 5g lab

q: Your smoke report is all green, but it has 22 rows where you expected 24. Pass or fail?
a: Fail, or at best incomplete. The pass rule explicitly requires that no antenna or flavour is silently missing. Build the expected matrix up front and reconcile against it. A missing row can mean a flavour that did not boot, an antenna whose playback never started, or a script that skipped a band.
tags: rct tx aclr evm measurements aau hardware lte 5g lab

q: Why is a pass on flavour 0 (B1B3) no evidence for flavour 2 (n41) on the same unit?
a: Each flavour is a separate FHGW personality with its own model name, start-up path, calibration data and RF chain. Real defects have hit one flavour only, for example a missing TX calibration file on B41 carriers because a start-up script did not recognise that model sub-variant. Test every flavour.
tags: rct tx aclr evm measurements aau hardware lte 5g lab

q: Why test 5 MHz separately on B3 and B28?
a: The narrower bandwidth uses a different filter and DPD setup, and customers may run it. Results at 10 or 15 MHz do not carry over. Bandwidth-dependent configuration has caused real defects on this platform, such as a DFE filter not following a runtime bandwidth change.
tags: rct tx aclr evm measurements aau hardware lte 5g lab

q: Why does ruauto run §6.3 before §6.4 and §6.5?
a: §6.3 measures Pmax per (band, freq, mod, trx_mode, ant, trx) and caches it for 1800 s. PvT needs Pmax (and a Pmin derived from it), and ORFS needs the carrier power reference. If §6.4 runs on its own, it measures Pmax inline.
tags: rct tx 2g measurements standards automation instruments troubleshooting debug

q: Your PvT mask verdict is Fail on bursts that look perfect, even with a very loose custom mask. What do you check?
a: Whether the custom mask is actually selected. The EXM defaults to EPVTime:MASK:SELect STANdard , so CLIMits:FAIL? evaluates the built-in Annex B mask. Send SELect CUSTom and CALC:EPVT:LIM:TEST ON , then read them back.
tags: rct tx 2g measurements standards automation instruments troubleshooting debug

q: What is the "useful part" of a GSM burst, and where is T0?
a: The 147 bits centred on T0, the transition between bits 13 and 14 of the 26-bit training sequence (midamble). Mean power and stability are computed over it. The analyzer finds T0 by TSC correlation, so an IMMediate trigger is fine.
tags: rct tx 2g measurements standards automation instruments troubleshooting debug

q: Two of four antennas read noise floor on Band 8 while OAM shows every carrier READY. How do you proceed?
a: Confirm the pattern follows the TRX/antenna and not the analyzer port. Check whether it also happens in single_trx. Then read the RU personality (per-band antenna bitmask in the CFR/DPD pulse config) and the RU operations-manager log for ModifyPA. If OAM is correct, collect PHY/L2 logs around activation. Rule out config-key misreads such as cable-loss port IDs before blaming calibration.
tags: rct tx 2g measurements standards automation instruments troubleshooting debug

q: Why can an out-of-band spurious test report "Info (TE noise-limited)" instead of Fail?
a: Limits like −98 dBm in the own RX band can sit below the analyzer floor for a single sweep. The harness adds the preamp and RMS averaging. If a reading is still at the instrument floor and the limit is below that floor, the result cannot be judged, so it is flagged Info rather than a false Fail. A reading clearly above the floor, like the −91.4 dBm RX-band leak, still fails.
tags: rct tx 2g measurements standards automation instruments troubleshooting debug

q: Where is the interferer placed in LTE in-band blocking for a 10 MHz channel?
a: Its centre frequency is stepped from the window edge (UL low − 20 MHz for most bands) up to 7.5 MHz below the wanted channel's lower edge. On the other side it runs from 7.5 MHz above the upper edge to UL high + 20 MHz. The 25 MHz zone around the wanted channel is excluded. The receiver must keep ≥95 % throughput with a −43 dBm 5 MHz interferer (Wide Area).
tags: rct rx measurements lte standards reference automation sensitivity

q: Why is the Band 8 upper window only +10 MHz?
a: Because the B8 downlink starts at 925 MHz, 10 MHz above the 915 MHz UL edge. The in-band window stops where the operator's own DL begins. Bands 26 and 28 are the same (Group B). Bands 20 and 71 have reversed duplex, so their lower side is shortened to −11 MHz instead.
tags: rct rx measurements lte standards reference automation sensitivity

q: B1 at 1950 MHz, 10 MHz BW: give the two interferer ranges.
a: Lower: 1900 to 1937.5 MHz. Upper: 1962.5 to 2000 MHz. Wanted channel 1945–1955, guard 1937.5–1962.5.
tags: rct rx measurements lte standards reference automation sensitivity

q: Blocking fails only at the offsets closest to the guard. What do you suspect first?
a: Check the test setup before the DUT: interferer generator ACLR/noise leaking into the wanted channel. Then check DUT linearity (LNA/ADC compression, IMD) and reciprocal mixing from LO phase noise. Compare against a run with a filtered interferer, and against the plain sensitivity result.
tags: rct rx measurements lte standards reference automation sensitivity

q: What does the TX ON/OFF power test check on an NR TDD BS, and what are the limits?
a: In UL periods the transmitter OFF power must be below −85 dBm/MHz, averaged over 70/N µs with N = SCS/15. The OFF→ON and ON→OFF transient periods must each be under 10 µs (LTE allows 17 µs). It protects the BS's own and neighbouring receivers in the UL slots.
tags: rct tx 5g nr measurements automation timing power aclr instruments standards

q: Your NR ACLR test passes at 32 dB. Is the radio conformant?
a: No. 32 dB passes the UE-style −30 dBc limit printed in the internal doc, but the BS requirement in 38.104 is 45 dB (or the absolute limit, if that is less stringent). Check which limit the KPI file actually applies.
tags: rct tx 5g nr measurements automation timing power aclr instruments standards

q: TAE comes back as −999. What happened?
a: −999 is the harness sentinel for "no valid TAE value in the MIMO table". Enable :SENS:RAD:MIMO:STAT 1 , make sure every chain is above about −30 dBm at the analyzer, and check the TDD trigger/gate. Then preset and re-read.
tags: rct tx 5g nr measurements automation timing power aclr instruments standards

q: Why does the PA-protection test poll for 25 s instead of reading once?
a: The 3 dB reduction appears after carrier activation. It lasts through a ~10 s gain-delay plateau, and the carrier itself can take up to ~15 s to become READY. A single timed read missed the dip whenever activation was slow. Polling and latching the deepest dip removes that race.
tags: rct tx 5g nr measurements automation timing power aclr instruments standards

q: How high must a conducted spurious sweep go for n78?
a: To the greater of 12.75 GHz and the 5th harmonic of the upper DL band edge. For n78 (3.8 GHz) that is 19 GHz, so a PXA/UXA-class analyzer is needed, not an EXM.
tags: rct tx 5g nr measurements automation timing power aclr instruments standards

q: How do clause 7 and clause 8 of TS 36.141 differ?
a: Clause 7 covers RF receiver characteristics with static, clean signals: sensitivity, dynamic range, selectivity, blocking, IMD. Clause 8 covers performance: demodulation of PUSCH/PUCCH/PRACH under multipath fading and noise at a defined SNR, with throughput or detection-probability metrics.
tags: rct rx lte 5g nr measurements standards reference phy prach

q: What do EPA5, EVA70 and ETU300 mean?
a: Channel model plus maximum Doppler. EPA is short delay spread (410 ns), EVA medium (2.5 µs), ETU long (5 µs). 5/70/300 Hz is the Doppler, i.e. how fast the fading varies. That relates to UE speed and carrier frequency.
tags: rct rx lte 5g nr measurements standards reference phy prach

q: What is the pass criterion for PUCCH format 1a ACK detection?
a: At the specified SNR, the ACK detection probability must be at least 0.99 when ACK is sent, and the false-detection probability at most 0.01 when only noise is present.
tags: rct rx lte 5g nr measurements standards reference phy prach

q: Why do the Type-A interference tests require an IRC receiver?
a: A dominant co-channel interferer on the same RBs cannot be removed by MRC, which only maximises the wanted SNR. IRC uses the interference covariance across the RX antennas to null it. With N RX antennas it can suppress up to N−1 strong interferers, hence 1 interferer for 2 RX and 2 for 4 or more RX.
tags: rct rx lte 5g nr measurements standards reference phy prach

q: Your PUSCH fading result is 8 points below the requirement. What do you check before blaming the PHY?
a: SNR calibration per RX branch (fader loss, AWGN level and bandwidth), fading correlation settings, generator headroom/clipping, and whether HARQ is really closed-loop. Then check the FRC and the channel-model configuration against the requirement table.
tags: rct rx lte 5g nr measurements standards reference phy prach

q: What is EIS and how do you measure it?
a: Equivalent isotropic sensitivity: the lowest power, referred to an ideal isotropic antenna at the DUT position, arriving from a given direction, at which the receiver still meets the reference throughput (BLER ≤ 5 %). You search the SG level down and subtract the calibrated path loss: EIS = SG min − PathLoss(f, az, el).
tags: rct measurements tx rx antenna lab calibration standards lte 5g sensitivity

q: Your chamber path loss is 75 dB and the EIS target is −101.5 dBm. What SG level do you set?
a: SG = EIS_target + PathLoss = −101.5 + 75 = −26.5 dBm, re-evaluated for each frequency and angle because the path loss changes.
tags: rct measurements tx rx antenna lab calibration standards lte 5g sensitivity

q: EIRP vs TRP: when is each used?
a: EIRP is directional (per beam or direction) and is used for radiated transmit power declarations. TRP is the sphere-integrated total and is used for OTA output power and for unwanted emissions (ACLR, OBUE, spurious), where interference to others does not depend on one direction.
tags: rct measurements tx rx antenna lab calibration standards lte 5g sensitivity

q: Why does a 1.6 m AAU need a compact range or near-field system?
a: The far-field distance 2D²/λ is about 12 m at 700 MHz for D = 1.6 m. That is far beyond a normal anechoic chamber. A compact antenna test range makes a plane wave with a reflector at short distance. Near-field scanning measures close in and transforms the result to far field.
tags: rct measurements tx rx antenna lab calibration standards lte 5g sensitivity

q: An OTA report shows ACLR = −47 dBc marked FAIL against a −45 dBc limit. Comment.
a: The verdict logic is inverted. −47 dBc means the adjacent channel is 47 dB below the carrier, which is better than the 45 dB requirement, so it passes. Compare magnitudes of the ratio, and fix the comparison in the harness.
tags: rct measurements tx rx antenna lab calibration standards lte 5g sensitivity

q: Why do you need a lab DC supply if the RU already reports its own power?
a: The RU measures PSU outputs and has to model the conversion losses. It also leaves out the common board and cabling. Only a supply on the chassis input sees the true total. It is the reference for calibrating and validating the RU's EPE POWER (CM14, GRDEV-9526).
tags: lab instruments power measurements python efficiency aau timing
