q: pyvisa fails to load visa32.dll on your laptop. What is the likely cause and fix?
a: A bitness mismatch: 64-bit Python needs visa64.dll. Install the 64-bit Keysight IO Libraries (or NI-VISA), pass the visa64.dll path to ResourceManager, or for a LAN instrument use the pure-Python backend: pip install pyvisa-py and ResourceManager("@py").
tags: lab instruments power measurements python efficiency aau timing

q: Your lab-supply average and the PM average disagree most at the start and end of each run. Why?
a: The windows are not aligned. The logger's minutes drift (sleep plus query time) and are not anchored to :00, while PM blocks are. During warm-up or load transitions, misaligned minutes compare different power levels. Bin both on wall-clock minutes and trim transitions.
tags: lab instruments power measurements python efficiency aau timing

q: What checks prove a 1-hour lab log is usable?
a: About 60 minutes present; at least 45 samples in each minute; no read errors or large gaps; an idle segment before RF; the warm-up excluded; the clock offset to the RU known; and the model confirmed by *IDN? rather than assumed from a label.
tags: lab instruments power measurements python efficiency aau timing

q: Why use a scanner in addition to test phones?
a: The phone only measures cells in its neighbour configuration and reports the served experience. The scanner decodes every cell on the channels independently, so it exposes missing neighbours, PCI collisions, pilot pollution, overshooting cells and external interference.
tags: instruments lab drive-test measurements ue optimization lte 5g

q: What must be true before you start logging a drive?
a: A GNSS 3D fix, all devices connected and stable (USB power saving off), a validated script, working SIMs and services, the correct RAT/band lock for the test purpose, and enough battery and disk.
tags: instruments lab drive-test measurements ue optimization lte 5g

q: Which NMEA sentences matter and what do they carry?
a: GGA (fix, altitude), RMC (minimum position/time), VTG (speed/course), GSA (DOP, satellites used) and GSV (satellites in view).
tags: instruments lab drive-test measurements ue optimization lte 5g

q: Your drive log shows a sudden drop with no RF degradation before it. What do you check?
a: Tool and device events first: USB disconnect, UE crash or reboot, overheating, battery, and time gaps in the log. Then the L3 trace around the event for a network release cause.
tags: instruments lab drive-test measurements ue optimization lte 5g

q: Scanner RSRP is 5 dB higher than the UE's. Is something wrong?
a: Not necessarily. Roof-mounted scanner antennas avoid in-car loss and have different gain. Compare trends and relative levels; only calibrated setups allow absolute comparison.
tags: instruments lab drive-test measurements ue optimization lte 5g

q: How is a PA switched off within one OFDM symbol on this board?
a: The FHGW's TX_EN line is ANDed with the MCU's MC_EN in a single-gate AND. The result drives three analog switches per path that move the driver, carrier and peaking gate biases of the GaN Doherty module to their off level. The drain supply stays up, so turn-on is only a gate swing. That is what makes symbol-rate uSleep possible.
tags: hardware aau rffe tx rx architecture power troubleshooting lab

q: The EPE CSV shows an RFFE drawing 0 A while its neighbour draws 1 A. Name three board-level causes.
a: The LM5069 hot-swap tripped or is disabled for that band group (over-current or over-voltage lockout at 57.5 V). The MCU has not enabled the supply (HS_EN). Or the telemetry path failed (current-sense amp / ADC), where you would see sentinels or zero while RF output is still present. Check with RF power measurement before blaming hardware.
tags: hardware aau rffe tx rx architecture power troubleshooting lab

q: Why do B20 and B28 share a TX path but not an RX path?
a: Their downlinks are adjacent (758–803 and 791–821 MHz), so one wideband TX line-up covers both. B20 has a reversed duplex: its uplink (832–862 MHz) sits next to B8's uplink (880–915 MHz). B28's uplink (703–748 MHz) is far below both. So the RX chains pair B8 with B20, and B28 gets its own.
tags: hardware aau rffe tx rx architecture power troubleshooting lab

q: What does the observation (OBS) path on the RFFE do, and what fails if it is wrong?
a: It couples a sample of each PA output, selects one path at a time with switches, phase-aligns it and sends it to the DPD observation receiver and a level detector. A wrong switch map or phase gives DPD the wrong feedback. You then see poor or drifting ACLR, or "DPD not aligned" pre-check failures, while the raw output power looks normal.
tags: hardware aau rffe tx rx architecture power troubleshooting lab

q: A5 is configured with threshold1 = 49, threshold2 = 40 and hysteresis 16. When does it trigger?
a: Convert first: 49 → −91 dBm, 40 → −100 dBm, hysteresis 16 → 8 dB. Entering needs Mp + 8 < −91 and Mn − 8 > −100 (ignoring offsets), so serving below −99 dBm and neighbour above −92 dBm, held for the TTT (0 here).
tags: lte-feature lte handover mobility measurements rsrp automation reference

q: What is the difference between A3 and A4, and between A5 and B2?
a: A3 is relative (neighbour better than serving plus an offset); A4 is absolute (neighbour above a threshold, serving ignored). A5 and B2 have the same two-threshold shape — serving bad AND neighbour good — but A5 targets another LTE frequency and B2 another RAT (UTRA/GERAN, or NR with B1/B2 in EN-DC).
tags: lte-feature lte handover mobility measurements rsrp automation reference

q: Why do VoLTE and mission-critical bearers get their own measurement policy?
a: Voice is sensitive to interruption and to late handovers, so operators want different thresholds, hysteresis and TTT for those UEs. The eNB applies the policy when the QCI 1 (or 65/66/69/70) bearer exists and must reconfigure the UE when the bearer is added — which is exactly what the tests check.
tags: lte-feature lte handover mobility measurements rsrp automation reference

q: How would you verify in a test that the eNB configured an event correctly?
a: Capture the RRCConnectionReconfiguration, filter on the event type, and compare each reportConfig field with the configured raw value (threshold index, hysteresis, TTT, interval, amount, max cells). Then drive the RF so the condition is met and check the MeasurementReport and the resulting HO messages.
tags: lte-feature lte handover mobility measurements rsrp automation reference

q: What does A1/A2 gating do and what goes wrong if the thresholds overlap?
a: A2 (serving bad) starts inter-frequency measurements with gaps, A1 (serving good) stops them to save throughput. If A1 is not above A2 plus twice the hysteresis, the UE oscillates between the two and gaps start and stop repeatedly.
tags: lte-feature lte handover mobility measurements rsrp automation reference

q: What is the difference between PSM and eDRX?
a: In PSM the UE is unreachable after T3324 expires and until its next TAU or uplink data, but stays attached; the MME does not page it at all. In eDRX the UE is still in idle mode and pageable, but only inside paging time windows separated by a long cycle (up to about 43 min in LTE).
tags: lte-feature lte ue efficiency call-flow fundamentals

q: What do T3324 and T3412 extended control?
a: T3324 is the active time: how long the UE stays pageable after going idle before entering PSM. T3412 extended is the periodic TAU timer, i.e. how long it can stay in PSM before it must check in. The UE requests both; the network grants the final values in Attach/TAU Accept.
tags: lte-feature lte ue efficiency call-flow fundamentals

q: How does a Cat-M UE choose its CE level?
a: It compares measured RSRP with up to three RSRP thresholds broadcast in system information and picks CE level 0-3. Each level has its own PRACH resources, repetition numbers and attempt limits; levels 0-1 are CE mode A, 2-3 CE mode B.
tags: lte-feature lte ue efficiency call-flow fundamentals

q: DL data arrives for a UE in PSM. What happens?
a: The MME knows the UE is unreachable and does not page it. The data is buffered in the core (if extended buffering is configured) or dropped, and delivered when the UE next wakes for a TAU or uplink data.
tags: lte-feature lte ue efficiency call-flow fundamentals

q: Why can deep coverage kill battery life even with PSM?
a: Because every message is repeated up to hundreds or thousands of times, so the awake/transmit time per report grows by one or two orders of magnitude. The sleep floor stays tiny, but the daily wake energy dominates.
tags: lte-feature lte ue efficiency call-flow fundamentals

q: What RSRP, RSRQ and SINR would you call good in LTE?
a: Typically RSRP better than about −90 dBm, RSRQ better than about −10 dB and SINR above about 13–15 dB. Stress that these are operator targets, not 3GPP limits, and depend on clutter and band.
tags: notes kpi measurements drive-test optimization reference troubleshooting lte 5g

q: RSRQ is −11 dB but SINR is 18 dB. Problem?
a: Probably not: RSRQ falls with cell load (about −10.8 dB at full load with no interference). With good SINR the cell is simply busy; check PRB utilisation.
tags: notes kpi measurements drive-test optimization reference troubleshooting lte 5g

q: BLER in the log is 10 %. Is the link bad?
a: No, link adaptation aims for about 10 % first-transmission BLER. Check residual BLER after HARQ and whether the MCS is appropriate for the SINR.
tags: notes kpi measurements drive-test optimization reference troubleshooting lte 5g

q: Why do two drive-test tools show different SINR at the same spot?
a: LTE UE SINR is not defined by 3GPP; each tool/chipset computes RS-SINR its own way. Compare trends within one tool and rely on RSRP/RSRQ for cross-tool comparisons.
tags: notes kpi measurements drive-test optimization reference troubleshooting lte 5g

q: What is the difference between PCI collision and PCI confusion?
a: Collision: two neighbouring cells use the same PCI, so a UE between them cannot tell them apart. Confusion: a serving cell has two different neighbours with the same PCI, so a measurement report is ambiguous and HO may go to the wrong cell.
tags: notes reference fundamentals lte 5g nr optimization antenna

q: What is MDT and why would an operator use it?
a: Minimisation of Drive Tests: the network configures UEs to log or report measurements (with location where available) and collects them, reducing the need for physical drive tests.
tags: notes reference fundamentals lte 5g nr optimization antenna

q: What are ABS and CRE?
a: eICIC tools: the macro transmits almost-blank subframes (only essential signals) while a cell range expansion bias pushes more users onto the small cell; those edge users are scheduled in the ABS.
tags: notes reference fundamentals lte 5g nr optimization antenna

q: What does SLIV encode?
a: The start symbol and length (in symbols) of a PDSCH or PUSCH time-domain allocation within a slot, as one index.
tags: notes reference fundamentals lte 5g nr optimization antenna

q: What is soft handover and why doesn't LTE use it?
a: In WCDMA the UE is connected to several NodeBs at once (active set) with macro-diversity combining at the RNC — natural in a reuse-1 CDMA system. LTE is OFDMA with independent per-cell scheduling and no RNC, so it uses hard HO with X2 forwarding; interference is managed by scheduling and ICIC.
tags: notes fundamentals handover mobility measurements reference lte

q: What separates cells vs channels in UMTS?
a: Downlink primary scrambling codes (512) separate cells; OVSF channelisation codes separate channels/users within a cell.
tags: notes fundamentals handover mobility measurements reference lte

q: Map RxLev, RSCP and RSRP.
a: All are received-level measurements: GSM RxLev (BCCH carrier level), UMTS CPICH RSCP (pilot code power), LTE RSRP (per-RE reference-signal power). Quality counterparts are RxQual, Ec/No and RSRQ/SINR.
tags: notes fundamentals handover mobility measurements reference lte

q: What does 577 µs / 4.615 ms mean in GSM?
a: One timeslot is about 577 µs; eight timeslots form a 4.615 ms TDMA frame on a 200 kHz carrier.
tags: notes fundamentals handover mobility measurements reference lte

q: How much downtime per year is 99.999 % availability?
a: About 5.26 minutes (0.001 % of 525 960 minutes).
tags: notes kpi fundamentals reference measurements

q: Write availability in terms of MTBF and MTTR. How would you improve it?
a: A = MTBF / (MTBF + MTTR). Increase MTBF (better hardware/software, fewer failures) or cut MTTR (faster detection, auto-recovery, spares, remote reset). Cutting MTTR is often cheaper.
tags: notes kpi fundamentals reference measurements

q: Two 99.9 % links in parallel — overall availability?
a: 1 − (0.001)² = 99.9999 %, if their failures are independent. In series it would be 99.8 %.
tags: notes kpi fundamentals reference measurements

q: A 72-hour stability run had zero failures. What MTBF have you demonstrated?
a: Only about 31 h at 90 % confidence (T / 2.30). Long MTBF claims need many unit-hours, accelerated testing or field data.
tags: notes kpi fundamentals reference measurements

q: How is overall accessibility calculated and why is it lower than each stage?
a: It is the product of the stage success rates: RRC setup × S1 signalling × E-RAB setup. Each stage can fail independently, so the product is below the weakest stage, e.g. 98.7 % × 99.8 % × 99.2 % ≈ 97.7 %.
tags: notes kpi lte 5g measurements troubleshooting reference

q: Write the E-RAB drop rate formula.
a: Abnormal active releases ÷ (abnormal active releases + normal active releases) × 100. Abnormal covers RLF, HO failure and network faults while data was pending; normal covers ordinary releases.
tags: notes kpi lte 5g measurements troubleshooting reference

q: How do you compute average user DL throughput from counters?
a: Sum the DRB IP volume and sum the active DL time (the time the buffer had data, excluding the last TTI of each burst), then divide: 1000 × Σvolume(kbit) ÷ Σtime(ms) gives kbps.
tags: notes kpi lte 5g measurements troubleshooting reference

q: Five cells show 99 %, 99 %, 98 %, 50 % and 99 % RRC success. Is the cluster KPI 89 %?
a: Not necessarily. Sum the successes and attempts over all cells and divide. If the 50 % cell had only a handful of attempts the cluster value is close to 99 %; averaging percentages is wrong.
tags: notes kpi lte 5g measurements troubleshooting reference

q: What does VoLTE UL packet loss measure and what causes it?
a: Lost QCI 1 PDCP SDUs in the uplink versus the number expected, from gaps in PDCP sequence numbers. Causes: HARQ and RLC retransmissions exhausted, PDCP discard timer expiry from scheduling delay, and poor UL coverage or interference.
tags: notes kpi lte 5g measurements troubleshooting reference

q: What is DSS and why do operators use it?
a: Dynamic Spectrum Sharing runs LTE and NR on the same carrier, with a scheduler dividing resources between them every subframe/slot. It gives fast NR coverage on existing LTE spectrum without stranding LTE-only phones or refarming.
tags: nr-nsa 5g nr lte endc architecture phy optimization

q: How does an NR UE avoid LTE's reference signals on a DSS carrier?
a: The gNB signals the LTE CRS pattern (lte-CRS-ToMatchAround: centre, bandwidth, ports, v-shift, MBSFN subframes). NR PDSCH is rate-matched around those REs. NR PDCCH is placed after LTE's control symbols, and SSB goes in MBSFN or CRS-free positions.
tags: nr-nsa 5g nr lte endc architecture phy optimization

q: What is the main cost of DSS?
a: Overhead. CRS rate matching alone costs about 9.5 % (2 ports) to 14 % (4 ports) of REs, plus the LTE control region and MBSFN impacts. NR capacity on DSS is lower than on the same bandwidth of dedicated spectrum, and scheduling is more complex.
tags: nr-nsa 5g nr lte endc architecture phy optimization

q: Why is DSS unusual on n78?
a: n78/n79 are mostly new TDD spectrum with no LTE to share with. DSS is mostly used on FDD bands where LTE is already deployed.
tags: nr-nsa 5g nr lte endc architecture phy optimization

q: How would you verify a DSS cell in the lab?
a: Check NR BLER and throughput with LTE CRS present, confirm LTE UE performance is unchanged, load each RAT separately and together to see the PRB split move, and confirm the SSB is found at the expected GSCN and subframes.
tags: nr-nsa 5g nr lte endc architecture phy optimization

q: What should happen on X2 when the CU of an en-gNB is rebooted?
a: The EN-DC X2 relation is removed (EN-DC X2 Removal) and the UE's SCG is released. When the CU is back, the eNB and gNB perform EN-DC X2 Setup again, and the next B1 report leads to a fresh SgNB Addition Request/Ack and SgNB Reconfiguration Complete, after which NR data resumes.
tags: nr-nsa 5g nr lte endc troubleshooting debug call-flow automation

q: Why inject faults with kill -11 rather than a clean stop?
a: A clean stop lets the process say goodbye (graceful SCTP shutdown, release messages). SIGSEGV simulates a real crash: peers see an SCTP ABORT or timeout, the pod's crash handling and restart run, and the recovery path — not the shutdown path — is tested.
tags: nr-nsa 5g nr lte endc troubleshooting debug call-flow automation

q: A resilience test passed but users complain that 5G takes minutes to return after a CU restart. Why did the test not catch it?
a: Because it waits a fixed time (up to 700 s) and then only checks that the recovery messages exist and that at least one byte of NR data passed. It measures eventual recovery, not recovery time or recovered throughput; add polling and timestamps to make it a KPI.
tags: nr-nsa 5g nr lte endc troubleshooting debug call-flow automation

q: What is special about an NSA-to-NSA handover?
a: The LTE anchor changes (X2 HO between eNBs) while the SCG must be released at the source and re-added at the target. The test checks the X2 HO Request/Ack and SN Status Transfer, then a new SgNB Addition at the target eNB, and that ENDC SgNB addition attempt and success counters are 1.
tags: nr-nsa 5g nr lte endc troubleshooting debug call-flow automation

q: An NSA UE stays on LTE. How do you troubleshoot it?
a: Walk the chain: did the eNB send an NR B1 measurement config; did the UE report B1; did the eNB send SgNB Addition Request; did the gNB acknowledge or reject; did the UE complete the SCG random access or send SCGFailureInformationNR? The first missing step points to LTE config/core restriction, NR frequency/coverage, neighbour/X2/PLMN, NR admission/transport, or the NR air interface respectively.
tags: nr-nsa 5g nr lte endc troubleshooting debug call-flow measurements

q: The UE reports B1 but no SgNB Addition Request is sent. Name three causes.
a: The reported NR PCI is not defined as a neighbour (or conflicts), the EN-DC X2 to that gNB is down, or the eNB's configured gNB PLMN / gNB ID does not match the gNB.
tags: nr-nsa 5g nr lte endc troubleshooting debug call-flow measurements

q: What does SCGFailureInformationNR with randomAccessProblem tell you?
a: The SgNB accepted and the UE was reconfigured, but it could not complete random access on the NR cell — an uplink problem (coverage, interference, PRACH configuration or power), not a DL or configuration-exchange problem.
tags: nr-nsa 5g nr lte endc troubleshooting debug call-flow measurements

q: Which counters would you look at first and why?
a: ENDC SgNB addition attempts and successes. Zero attempts means the eNB never requested a leg (stages 1-3); attempts without successes means the gNB rejected or the UE failed on NR (stages 4-5). NR byte counters confirm that added legs carry traffic.
tags: nr-nsa 5g nr lte endc troubleshooting debug call-flow measurements

q: Why can the NR RSRP be excellent while EN-DC still fails?
a: B1 is a downlink measurement. The SCG must also close the uplink, often on a higher-frequency TDD carrier with less UL budget than LTE. Strong DL with weak UL gives SgNB addition followed by SCG RACH failure.
tags: nr-nsa 5g nr lte endc troubleshooting debug call-flow measurements

q: How do you trigger a handover in an automated lab test without moving the UE?
a: With programmable attenuators on each cell's RF path. Start with the source strong and the target at maximum attenuation, then step the target down and the source up (here 2 dB every 200 ms on all four antennas). The UE sees the target become better than the serving cell by the A3 offset for the time-to-trigger, reports it, and the network runs the HO on its own — so the whole decision chain is tested, not just the execution.
tags: nr-sa 5g nr handover call-flow protocol automation debug

q: Which IEs would you check to prove an Xn handover really happened end to end?
a: Cause handover-desirable-for-radio-reasons in the XnAP HandoverRequest; SpCell-ID and SRB/DRB IDs in the target's F1AP UE Context Setup Request; the Target-to-Source transparent container (the RRC HO command) in the HO Ack; an SN Status Transfer; a Path Switch Request/Ack whose AMF-UE-NGAP-ID equals the source's (same UE context in the core); and the source releasing the UE with normal-release.
tags: nr-sa 5g nr handover call-flow protocol automation debug

q: Why must ciphering be NEA0 for this kind of test?
a: Because the checks decode RRC content (measId, neighbour PCI, CGI, HO command) carried inside F1AP/XnAP. With ciphering on, that payload is encrypted in the capture and the assertions cannot see it. It is a test-visibility requirement, not a product requirement.
tags: nr-sa 5g nr handover call-flow protocol automation debug

q: Give two negative Xn HO tests and their expected outcomes.
a: HO not allowed on the neighbour relation: no HandoverRequest is sent at all. Hand-in disabled on the target: the target answers with HandoverPreparationFailure, cause handover-target-not-allowed, and the source's prep-failure-target-not-allowed counter equals its hand-out attempts.
tags: nr-sa 5g nr handover call-flow protocol automation debug

q: The test failed with NO_PACKETS on the HandoverRequest filter although Xn is up. Where do you look?
a: At the radio trigger, not Xn: was the neighbour added with the correct SSB ARFCN, did the UE get a measConfig for it, did a MeasurementReport arrive, did the attenuators actually move, and is the UE still attached? Only if a report arrived and no request followed is it a CU decision problem (neighbour relation hoallowed, Xn TNL, admission).
tags: nr-sa 5g nr handover call-flow protocol automation debug

q: What is the difference between HO preparation success and execution success?
a: Preparation is network-to-network: the target accepted and returned the HO command (Attempt → PrepSuccess). Execution is the UE part: after receiving the command the UE synchronises and completes on the target (ExeAttempt → Success). Prep failures point to admission or config; execution failures point to radio (RACH, RLF, T304).
tags: nr-sa 5g nr handover kpi automation call-flow

q: How does the inter-CU CI compute the handover success rate?
a: It captures NGAP/F1AP on both CUs during 20 attenuation swings with 8 UEs, counts HandoverRequired (source side) and HandoverNotify (target side) in both directions, and computes 100 × ΣNotify / ΣRequired rounded to 3 decimals. It passes at 85 % or more and fails separately if no HandoverRequired was seen.
tags: nr-sa 5g nr handover kpi automation call-flow

q: Why derive expected counter values from the packet capture instead of hard-coding them?
a: So the test stays correct when the radio produces more than one HO (ping-pong) and still checks that the counters match what really happened. The trade-off is that a capture gap affects both sides, so it complements, not replaces, a sanity check on absolute numbers.
tags: nr-sa 5g nr handover kpi automation call-flow

q: Hand-in is disabled on the target. Which counters should move?
a: Source: XnHandOutAttempt and XnHandOutPrepFailureTargetNotAllowed by the same amount, no PrepSuccess. Target: XnHandInAttempt and XnHandInPrepFailure by the same amount. The Xn message is HandoverPreparationFailure with cause handover-target-not-allowed.
tags: nr-sa 5g nr handover kpi automation call-flow

q: How many PCIs are there in LTE and NR, and how are they built?
a: LTE: 504 = 168 SSS groups × 3 PSS sequences. NR: 1008 = 336 × 3. In both, PCI = 3·N_ID(1) + N_ID(2).
tags: protocol lte 5g nr optimization phy handover drive-test troubleshooting

q: Why must neighbouring cells have different PCI mod 3?
a: Mod 3 selects the PSS sequence and, in LTE with 2 or 4 CRS ports, the CRS frequency shift. Equal values put the reference signals on the same REs, so RSRQ, SINR and channel estimation degrade even at low load.
tags: protocol lte 5g nr optimization phy handover drive-test troubleshooting

q: What does PCI mod 30 affect?
a: The UL DMRS / PUCCH base-sequence group. Neighbours with equal mod 30 have correlated UL reference signals, which hurts UL channel estimation.
tags: protocol lte 5g nr optimization phy handover drive-test troubleshooting

q: Explain PCI collision versus confusion, and how the network detects them.
a: Collision: two overlapping cells share a PCI. Confusion: one cell has two neighbours with the same PCI, so the HO target is ambiguous. ANR detects both when a UE reports a CGI different from the one stored for that PCI; SON or the operator then re-assigns.
tags: protocol lte 5g nr optimization phy handover drive-test troubleshooting

q: A drive test shows RSRP −80 dBm but SINR −2 dB. How would you check if PCI is involved?
a: Look at the scanner's top-N list. The same PCI from two CGIs means collision. A strong neighbour with the same mod 3 means an RS collision. If neither applies, suspect overshoot, pilot pollution or external interference.
tags: protocol lte 5g nr optimization phy handover drive-test troubleshooting

q: Write the PUSCH power-control formula and explain each term.
a: P = min{P_CMAX, P0 + 10·log10(2^μ·M_RB) + α·PL + Δ_TF + f(i)}. P0 is the target per RB, the bandwidth term keeps power per RB constant, α·PL is the fractional path-loss compensation, Δ_TF is the MCS offset and f(i) is the accumulated closed-loop TPC. The result is capped at P_CMAX.
tags: protocol lte 5g nr phy ue power optimization

q: Why is α less than 1 in many networks?
a: Fractional compensation lets edge UEs transmit a little less than full compensation would require. That limits UL interference (IoT) in neighbour cells and usually raises average cell throughput, at a small edge-SINR cost. PUCCH always uses α = 1.
tags: protocol lte 5g nr phy ue power optimization

q: What are the TPC step values?
a: Accumulated mode is {−1, 0, +1, +3} dB. Absolute mode is {−4, −1, +1, +4} dB. LTE DCI 3A uses 1-bit ±1 dB.
tags: protocol lte 5g nr phy ue power optimization

q: What is PHR and how is it used?
a: Power headroom = P_CMAX minus the power the UE would need for the current allocation, reported in a MAC CE periodically or when path loss changes. Negative PHR means the UE is power-limited, so the scheduler reduces RBs or MCS instead of asking for power the UE does not have.
tags: protocol lte 5g nr phy ue power optimization

q: UL BLER is high only at the cell edge while DL is fine. What do you check?
a: PHR and UE TX power (is it at P_CMAX?), P0/α settings, TPC behaviour, UL interference (IoT per PRB), UL sensitivity of the receiver, and whether the DL power makes the cell bigger than its UL can support.
tags: protocol lte 5g nr phy ue power optimization

q: CSSR is low on one cell. How do you break it down?
a: Split it by stage (RRC vs E-RAB/PDU), by hour and by cause code. Then check coverage/UL limits, interference, admission/congestion counters, RACH performance, core rejects and hardware alarms. Confirm with a drive-test L3 trace at the failure locations.
tags: protocol optimization drive-test kpi lte 5g troubleshooting measurements

q: What is the difference between a setup failure and a drop?
a: A setup failure means the connection never completed (accessibility). A drop is an abnormal release of a connection that was established successfully (retainability). The formula (attempts − successes)/attempts is setup failure rate, not drop rate.
tags: protocol optimization drive-test kpi lte 5g troubleshooting measurements

q: How do you plan a drive-test route for a new cluster?
a: Use the site database and maps. Cross every sector footprint and every handover border, cover main roads plus some side streets, keep the route continuous, drive both directions for HO checks, and keep a steady 20–40 km/h in town with logging only after GNSS lock.
tags: protocol optimization drive-test kpi lte 5g troubleshooting measurements

q: After changing a tilt, how do you validate it?
a: Re-drive the same route with the same setup and compare it with the baseline. Then watch the cell's and its neighbours' KPIs for several days to confirm the improvement and that no neighbour degraded. Keep a rollback plan.
tags: protocol optimization drive-test kpi lte 5g troubleshooting measurements

q: Throughput is low at a point where RSRP is −78 dBm. What next?
a: Check SINR and CQI first: poor SINR means interference. If SINR is good, check PRB utilisation and user count (load), then MIMO rank and CA status, then backhaul and core. RSRP alone does not predict throughput.
tags: protocol optimization drive-test kpi lte 5g troubleshooting measurements

q: Convert LTE band 3 downlink 1850 MHz to an EARFCN, and give the UL.
a: N_DL = 1200 + (1850 − 1805)/0.1 = 1650. The UL EARFCN is 19650, which is 1755 MHz.
tags: protocol lte 5g nr fundamentals reference phy

q: What is the NR-ARFCN of 3600 MHz?
a: It is in the 3–24.25 GHz range with a 15 kHz raster: 600000 + (3600 − 3000)/0.015 = 640000.
tags: protocol lte 5g nr fundamentals reference phy

q: How are ECI and NCI built?
a: ECI is 28 bits: a 20-bit eNB ID plus an 8-bit cell ID. NCI is 36 bits: a gNB ID of 22–32 bits plus the cell ID in the remaining bits. Prefix either with the PLMN to get the global ECGI/NCGI.
tags: protocol lte 5g nr fundamentals reference phy

q: How big is the TAC in LTE and NR?
a: 16 bits in LTE and 24 bits in NR.
tags: protocol lte 5g nr fundamentals reference phy

q: What is the difference between PCI and ECGI?
a: PCI is a short physical-layer label (504 or 1008 values) reused across the network. ECGI/NCGI is globally unique. ANR asks the UE to read the CGI when it needs to resolve which cell a PCI really is.
tags: protocol lte 5g nr fundamentals reference phy

q: Why does the first REGISTER always get a 401 — is that a failure?
a: No. It is the normal digest-AKA challenge. The S-CSCF sends RAND and AUTN in the nonce; the ISIM verifies the network and computes RES; the second REGISTER carries the response and gets 200 OK. A failure is a second 401 or a 403 after the response.
tags: protocol lte call-flow debug troubleshooting ue

q: At which SIP message is the QCI 1 bearer created and why there?
a: Around the 183 Session Progress, when the P-CSCF has seen both the SDP offer and answer and knows the media 5-tuple and bandwidth. It sends Rx to the PCRF, which triggers the dedicated bearer. Preconditions make the far end wait with ringing until both sides have their bearer.
tags: protocol lte call-flow debug troubleshooting ue

q: What are PRACK and UPDATE for in VoLTE?
a: PRACK acknowledges a reliable provisional response (the 183 with RSeq), so the SDP answer cannot be silently lost. UPDATE tells the far end mid-setup that the local QoS precondition is now met, so B can start ringing (180) knowing voice will work.
tags: protocol lte call-flow debug troubleshooting ue

q: Which bearer carries SIP and which carries RTP?
a: SIP runs on the default bearer of the IMS PDN (QCI 5, non-GBR, high priority). RTP/RTCP voice runs on a dedicated QCI 1 GBR bearer created per call and removed after BYE.
tags: protocol lte call-flow debug troubleshooting ue

q: A VoLTE call fails with 580 Precondition Failure. Where do you look on the RAN side?
a: At the QCI 1 E-RAB Setup: did the eNB admit it, or put it in the failed list (admission control, GBR licence, ARP)? Was the RRC Reconfiguration completed? If the RAN accepted it, look at the PCRF/Rx/Gx side.
tags: protocol lte call-flow debug troubleshooting ue

q: What is the difference between EPS attach and combined EPS/IMSI attach?
a: EPS attach registers only for packet services. Combined also registers the UE in the CS domain through the SGs interface to the MSC/VLR, which is needed for CSFB voice and SMS over SGs. The Attach Accept then includes an LAI and TMSI, and the attach result says "combined".
tags: protocol lte 5g call-flow debug ue reference

q: A UE sends a switch-off detach and no Detach Accept comes back. Bug?
a: No. With the switch-off bit set, the network does not answer because the UE is powering down. The MME just releases the S1 context (UE Context Release Command with NAS cause detach).
tags: protocol lte 5g call-flow debug ue reference

q: List the 5GS registration types.
a: Initial (1), mobility registration updating (2), periodic registration updating (3), emergency (4), and in Rel-17 SNPN onboarding (5) and two disaster-roaming types (6, 7). The follow-on request and SMS-over-NAS indications are separate flags, not types.
tags: protocol lte 5g call-flow debug ue reference

q: A UE's TAU is rejected with cause #10 after the core was restarted. What happened?
a: The MME lost or implicitly detached the UE context, so it cannot accept the TAU. The UE must perform a new attach. Expect a burst of these after a core restart, together with full attaches with authentication.
tags: protocol lte 5g call-flow debug ue reference

q: Which NAS timer would you suspect when an attach attempt repeats every 10 s and then stops for 12 minutes?
a: T3411 (10 s retry between attempts) and, after five failed attempts, T3402 (12 min back-off). Check the reject cause or the missing Attach Accept that caused the retries.
tags: protocol lte 5g call-flow debug ue reference

q: When does an eNB choose S1 instead of X2 handover?
a: When there is no X2 to the target, X2 handover is barred for that neighbour, the X2 preparation failed, or the target is served by a different MME (or needs an S-GW change the eNBs cannot handle). The S1 path is always available because every eNB has S1 to its MME.
tags: protocol lte call-flow handover mobility debug troubleshooting

q: What is inside the Handover Request that the target eNB really needs?
a: The E-RABs to set up with QoS and the S-GW UL TEIDs, UE-AMBR, the UE security capabilities and the {NCC, NH} security context, the handover restriction list, and the source-to-target container with the UE capability and current radio config.
tags: protocol lte call-flow handover mobility debug troubleshooting

q: What is indirect data forwarding and when is it used?
a: DL data is forwarded source eNB → S-GW → target eNB through temporary GTP tunnels created with Create Indirect Data Forwarding Tunnel, used when the source and target have no direct IP path. They are deleted after the handover completes.
tags: protocol lte call-flow handover mobility debug troubleshooting

q: Why is eNB/MME Status Transfer needed?
a: It passes the PDCP COUNT (HFN + SN) of each RLC AM bearer to the target, so the target continues the same numbering for ciphering and delivers in order without loss or duplicates.
tags: protocol lte call-flow handover mobility debug troubleshooting

q: How does security differ between X2 and S1 handover?
a: In S1 the MME provides a fresh NH with an incremented NCC, so the target key is derived from material the source never had. In X2 the source usually derives KeNB* from its own key, so the source can in principle compute the target key.
tags: protocol lte call-flow handover mobility debug troubleshooting

q: What is the difference between immediate and logged MDT?
a: Immediate MDT collects measurements from connected UEs in real time through normal measurement reports plus base-station measurements. Logged MDT configures a UE to record measurements while idle (or inactive in NR) and hand the log over later, when it reconnects and the network requests it.
tags: protocol lte 5g measurements drive-test kpi optimization ue

q: Name the MDT measurements M1 to M7.
a: M1 RSRP/RSRQ, M2 power headroom, M3 received interference power, M4 data volume, M5 scheduled IP throughput, M6 packet delay, M7 packet loss rate.
tags: protocol lte 5g measurements drive-test kpi optimization ue

q: You see S1AP CellTrafficTrace in a capture. What does it mean?
a: A trace (often an MDT job) is active for that UE. The eNB reports the trace reference, cell ID and collector address to the MME so the collector can link the trace records to the subscriber identity.
tags: protocol lte 5g measurements drive-test kpi optimization ue

q: Management-based vs signalling-based MDT?
a: Management-based is configured by OAM for an area and the eNB chooses consenting UEs there. Signalling-based targets one subscriber via the HSS and MME and follows the UE across cells.
tags: protocol lte 5g measurements drive-test kpi optimization ue

q: Can MDT replace drive testing completely?
a: No. It gives continuous coverage and quality data from real users, including indoors, but it cannot test a network before users exist, cannot run scripted calls or benchmark competitors, and location accuracy depends on the UE.
tags: protocol lte 5g measurements drive-test kpi optimization ue

q: Your filter shows no X2AP in an eNB capture, but handovers clearly happened. What do you check?
a: Whether the filter excluded it. Use sctp.data_payload_proto_id == 27 or x2ap , not an ip -based filter, because X2 is often on IPv6 or another VLAN. Check the protocol hierarchy for SCTP under IPv6, and check that a non-standard X2 port is decoded (Decode As). In the lab captures on this card X2 was on IPv6, and an IPv4-only check reported "no X2AP" by mistake.
tags: protocol debug handover call-flow lte troubleshooting

q: Write the A3 entering condition and name each term.
a: Mn + Ofn + Ocn − Hys > Mp + Ofp + Ocp + Off, held for TTT. Mn/Mp = neighbour/serving measurement, Ofn/Ofp = frequency offsets, Ocn/Ocp = cell individual offsets, Hys = hysteresis, Off = a3-Offset.
tags: protocol handover mobility optimization kpi troubleshooting debug lte 5g

q: HOs are happening too late on a highway. What do you change?
a: Confirm with the RLF/re-establishment pattern (RLF in source, re-establish in target). Then lower TTT (e.g. 320 → 160 or 80 ms), reduce Off/Hys, or raise the CIO of the target on that relation. Check for missing neighbours first. Re-drive at the same speed.
tags: protocol handover mobility optimization kpi troubleshooting debug lte 5g

q: Ping-pong between two cells, no drops — fix?
a: Increase hysteresis and/or TTT on that pair. If it persists, the overlap is too large: tilt or reduce power on one cell. CIO can shift the boundary away from where slow users sit.
tags: protocol handover mobility optimization kpi troubleshooting debug lte 5g

q: What is the difference between hysteresis and a3-Offset?
a: Both add dB to the entering bar, but hysteresis also applies (with the opposite sign) to the leaving condition, creating a dead-band that suppresses oscillation. Offset only moves the boundary.
tags: protocol handover mobility optimization kpi troubleshooting debug lte 5g

q: Why is CIO preferred for fixing a single bad relation?
a: It is per-neighbour and directional, so it changes one boundary without affecting every other HO of the cell, unlike Off, Hys or TTT which apply to the whole report configuration.
tags: protocol handover mobility optimization kpi troubleshooting debug lte 5g

q: What is pilot pollution? Is it the same as two cells sharing a PCI?
a: No. Pilot pollution is too many cells of similar strength (typically four or more within about 5–6 dB of the best) with no dominant server, so SINR collapses despite good RSRP. Same PCI on nearby cells is PCI collision/confusion — an identity problem fixed by re-planning PCIs.
tags: protocol optimization drive-test kpi troubleshooting debug antenna lte 5g

q: How do you prove a cell is overshooting?
a: Serving-cell plot showing it serving far outside its tier, scanner top-N showing it strong inside other cells, a long TA tail in PM counters (≈ 78 m per LTE TA step), and RSRP that is abnormally high at distance with poor SINR. Then check tilt, height, power and terrain.
tags: protocol optimization drive-test kpi troubleshooting debug antenna lte 5g

q: RSRP −80 dBm but SINR −2 dB. Coverage or interference? Next step?
a: Interference. Look at scanner top-N: one strong far cell → overshoot; a flat group → pollution; check PCI mod 3 of the strongest neighbours; if the DL is clean but UL is bad, hunt external interference with a spectrum analyser.
tags: protocol optimization drive-test kpi troubleshooting debug antenna lte 5g

q: Why is electrical tilt preferred over mechanical tilt for an overshoot fix?
a: Electrical tilt tilts the whole pattern uniformly (and can be done remotely by RET/AISG). Mechanical tilt lowers only the front lobe, raises the back lobe and widens the horizontal pattern at the sides.
tags: protocol optimization drive-test kpi troubleshooting debug antenna lte 5g

q: Throughput is 2–3 Mbps at RSRP −75 dBm. What do you check?
a: SINR and CQI first (interference?), then PRB utilisation and number of users (load?), scheduler limits, CA/MIMO rank, then backhaul and server. Good RSRP rules out coverage, not interference or congestion.
tags: protocol optimization kpi troubleshooting debug drive-test lte 5g nr

q: NSA users are rarely on 5G. Where do you look?
a: B1 threshold and NR measurement config on the LTE anchor, NR neighbour definitions, X2 to the gNB, SgNB addition success/failure causes, UE band-combination capability, and NR-leg coverage/SINR.
tags: protocol optimization kpi troubleshooting debug drive-test lte 5g nr

q: Ping is 120 ms but radio KPIs and throughput are fine. Cause?
a: Transport or core: backhaul congestion/routing, far core/UPF, test-server location. Confirm by pinging from the site router/transport side vs from the UE; fix routing/capacity/QoS.
tags: protocol optimization kpi troubleshooting debug drive-test lte 5g nr

q: A cell has PRB 98–100 % in the busy hour. Options?
a: Short term: load balancing to neighbours/other layers, CA. Long term: add a carrier, sector split (3 → 6), small cells. Parameter tuning does not create capacity.
tags: protocol optimization kpi troubleshooting debug drive-test lte 5g nr

q: How do you present an optimisation result in an interview?
a: STAR: the KPI and where/when, the target, the evidence-driven checks and single-step changes, and the before/after numbers including a check that neighbouring cells did not degrade.
tags: protocol optimization kpi troubleshooting debug drive-test lte 5g nr

q: What MOS and R-factor do you expect for good VoLTE?
a: MOS ≥ 4.0 with AMR-WB, i.e. R about 80 or more. R ≥ 70 (MOS ≈ 3.6) is the usual "acceptable" floor. Measured in the field with POLQA (P.863).
tags: protocol drive-test kpi troubleshooting debug measurements call-flow lte 5g

q: A user can hear the other party but is not heard. How do you debug?
a: It is one-way audio: check RTP packet counters per direction at each hop (UE, RAN GTP-U, SBC). Check the SDP IP/port, NAT/firewall pinholes at the SBC, that the UL dedicated bearer/TFT exists, and ROHC context. The direction where packets stop is the fault location.
tags: protocol drive-test kpi troubleshooting debug measurements call-flow lte 5g

q: What is SIP Timer B and what happens when it expires?
a: The INVITE client transaction timeout, 64 × T1 = 32 s with RFC 3261 defaults (IMS UE side often T1 = 2 s → 128 s). On expiry the transaction fails as a timeout (408) and the call attempt fails.
tags: protocol drive-test kpi troubleshooting debug measurements call-flow lte 5g

q: Why does a 401 during IMS registration not mean failure?
a: It is the normal authentication challenge: the S-CSCF returns 401 with the AKA challenge, and the UE re-sends REGISTER with the response; 200 OK completes registration.
tags: protocol drive-test kpi troubleshooting debug measurements call-flow lte 5g

q: Why is bursty packet loss worse than the same average random loss?
a: Packet-loss concealment handles isolated losses well, but consecutive lost frames (e.g. during a HO gap) produce audible dropouts; the E-model's Ie,eff grows faster with burstiness.
tags: protocol drive-test kpi troubleshooting debug measurements call-flow lte 5g

q: Why run UDP before TCP in a throughput test?
a: UDP shows what the radio and transport can carry without TCP congestion control. If UDP reaches the expected rate but TCP does not, the limit is TCP window, RTT, loss or the server — not the RAN.
tags: protocol drive-test measurements kpi troubleshooting debug efficiency lte 5g

q: One TCP stream gives 13 Mbit/s over a link with 40 ms RTT. Why?
a: Window-limited: 64 KB ÷ 40 ms ≈ 13 Mbit/s. Enable window scaling or use parallel streams (iperf3 -P).
tags: protocol drive-test measurements kpi troubleshooting debug efficiency lte 5g

q: Good RSRP, good SINR, but low throughput. What next?
a: Check scheduled PRBs and cell load/users, CA and rank state, UE category, TDD pattern, then backhaul utilisation, core and server; compare the measured rate with the TPUT01 ceiling at the logged MCS and rank.
tags: protocol drive-test measurements kpi troubleshooting debug efficiency lte 5g

q: What does iperf3 -R do?
a: Reverse mode: the server sends and the client receives, so with the client on the UE it measures downlink.
tags: protocol drive-test measurements kpi troubleshooting debug efficiency lte 5g

q: BLER is 10 % in the log. Is that a problem?
a: Not by itself: link adaptation deliberately targets about 10 % first-transmission BLER for efficiency. Look at residual BLER after HARQ and at whether MCS is dropping.
tags: protocol drive-test measurements kpi troubleshooting debug efficiency lte 5g

q: How do you analyse a single call drop in a drive-test log?
a: Locate time and position, list events in the preceding 10–20 s, read Layer-3 (last Measurement Report, HO command, re-establishment cause), take the RF snapshot 5–10 s before (serving and neighbour RSRP/SINR, CQI, BLER, UE TX power), then classify: coverage, HO failure, congestion, core/transport, UE or configuration.
tags: protocol drive-test troubleshooting debug optimization kpi handover lte 5g

q: Good RSRP but poor SINR on a route. First thing you look at?
a: Scanner top-N at those points: a single strong distant cell suggests overshoot; several cells within a few dB suggests pilot pollution; then check PCI mod 3 of the strongest neighbours and whether SINR tracks load.
tags: protocol drive-test troubleshooting debug optimization kpi handover lte 5g

q: Why is a drive log alone not enough for RCA?
a: It is one UE on one route at one time. Confirm with PM counters (all users), a scanner (all cells), alarms and a repeat drive; correlate RF, Layer-3 and KPI.
tags: protocol drive-test troubleshooting debug optimization kpi handover lte 5g

q: After a tilt change the drop rate in the target cell improved. Are you done?
a: No: re-drive the same route, check the 5th-percentile RSRP for new holes, watch neighbouring cells' KPIs for a few days, and document before/after.
tags: protocol drive-test troubleshooting debug optimization kpi handover lte 5g

q: Where is the RRC message that tells the UE to hand over, in an X2 capture?
a: Inside the X2AP HandoverRequestAcknowledge, in the TargeteNBtoSource-eNBTransparentContainer. It holds an RRC HandoverCommand wrapping the RRCConnectionReconfiguration with mobilityControlInfo. The target builds it; the source only forwards it to the UE.
tags: protocol debug handover call-flow lte troubleshooting

q: What is in SN Status Transfer and why does it matter?
a: For each AM bearer, the UL and DL COUNT (PDCP SN plus HFN), optionally with a bitmap of missing UL PDCP SDUs. The target continues ciphering from that COUNT and delivers data in order without loss or duplicates. A wrong or missing value causes deciphering errors or data loss after the HO.
tags: protocol debug handover call-flow lte troubleshooting

q: HO Request to Ack took 26-44 ms and Path Switch to Ack 0.3 ms. What does each number measure?
a: The first is target eNB processing: admission control and building the RRC reconfiguration. The second is the core: MME plus SGW moving the S1-U path. Neither is the user-plane interruption time, which is measured at the UE from the RRC Reconfiguration to RRC Reconfiguration Complete.
tags: protocol debug handover call-flow lte troubleshooting

q: The HO command has ra-PreambleIndex 53 and the cell uses 52 preambles. So what?
a: Preambles 0-51 are for contention-based access, so 53 is one of the reserved dedicated preambles. The UE does contention-free random access on the target, which is faster and avoids collisions. If the dedicated preamble were inside the contention range, two UEs could collide during the HO.
tags: protocol debug handover call-flow lte troubleshooting

q: What does nextHopChainingCount = 0 in the HO Request tell you?
a: No fresh Next Hop key has been provided yet, so the target key KeNB* is derived horizontally from the current KeNB. After the Path Switch, the MME returns a new NH with NCC = 1 so the next HO can use vertical derivation.
tags: protocol debug handover call-flow lte troubleshooting

q: Who sends an X2 RLF Indication, to whom, and why?
a: The eNB where the UE re-established sends it to the eNB that owns the cell where the radio link failed. It carries the failure-cell PCI, the re-establishment cell ECGI, the old C-RNTI, ShortMAC-I and the re-establishment cause, so the owner can classify the failure for MRO (too early, too late, wrong cell).
tags: protocol debug troubleshooting handover mobility call-flow lte kpi

q: Why does a HandoverRequest follow the RLF Indication within 3 ms in the capture?
a: The failure-cell owner pushes the UE context to the eNB where the UE re-established, using the HO preparation, so the re-establishment can succeed and the call survives. LTE X2 has no dedicated context-fetch procedure, so this is vendor behaviour built on standard messages.
tags: protocol debug troubleshooting handover mobility call-flow lte kpi

q: The SN Status Transfer comes after UE Context Release. Why is that a problem?
a: UE Context Release means the handover is finished and the source can delete the UE. The COUNTs must reach the target before it starts PDCP on the new bearers. Arriving afterwards (here also with a UE ID that matches nothing), they are ignored, which risks loss, duplicates or ciphering errors on the re-established bearers.
tags: protocol debug troubleshooting handover mobility call-flow lte kpi

q: How do you prove an ordering defect is real and not a capture artefact?
a: Capture at both ends and check the same order appears in both, check the SCTP TSNs (sending order), check it repeats every time in the same scenario, and compare with a scenario where it is correct (here the reverse direction). Then attach frame numbers and filters to the bug.
tags: protocol debug troubleshooting handover mobility call-flow lte kpi

q: What does RRCConnReestabIndicator = otherFailure mean for MRO?
a: The UE re-established after a radio link failure, not after a failed handover or reconfiguration. With no recent HO into the failure cell this points to a too-late HO toward the re-establishment cell.
tags: protocol debug troubleshooting handover mobility call-flow lte kpi

q: What is the difference between an s1-Interface and a partOfS1-Interface Reset?
a: s1-Interface resets everything: all UE-associated connections on that S1 are released. partOfS1-Interface lists specific UEs by their S1AP IDs, and only those are released. Either side can send it, and the receiver answers with ResetAcknowledge.
tags: protocol debug troubleshooting call-flow lte kpi architecture

q: Service Request success is 50 % but there are no InitialContextSetupFailures. How?
a: The failures happen before ICS. The core answers the Service Request with a per-UE Reset, so no ICS is ever attempted. The UE retries after T3417 (5 s) and then succeeds. Count Service Requests against ICS Responses, not ICS Requests against Responses.
tags: protocol debug troubleshooting call-flow lte kpi architecture

q: What should an eNB do when it receives S1SetupFailure with TimeToWait = 20 s?
a: Wait at least 20 s before sending another S1SetupRequest to that MME. In the capture it retried after exactly 20.000 s and succeeded. Retrying sooner would violate TS 36.413 and add load to an MME that is recovering.
tags: protocol debug troubleshooting call-flow lte kpi architecture

q: Why do TAU and Service rejects with cause #9 appear after a core reset?
a: Cause #9 means the network cannot derive the UE identity: the core lost the context behind the UE's GUTI. The UE deletes its GUTI and security context and re-attaches with IMSI, which is why full attaches with Authentication and Security Mode follow.
tags: protocol debug troubleshooting call-flow lte kpi architecture

q: How do you decide whether a Reset storm is the eNB's fault?
a: Check who sends the Resets, their cause class, and what happens just before them. Resets from the core with a transport cause, no eNB-initiated releases before them, prompt ResetAcks and correct TimeToWait handling all point away from the eNB and toward the core or transport.
